top_candidates.title: title: Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF) — Launch & Operations Manual Overview This document describes the Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF), an opt-in program that supports cross-team skills development, rapid onboarding into adjacent domains, and internal mobility at Redwood. The RPF is a 6–12 week, project-oriented rotation designed for ICs and early managers who want hands-on experience in a different product area, platform team, or customer success track while keeping their core role and compensation intact. Purpose and goals - Accelerate skill acquisition for high-impact, cross-functional projects. - Reduce time-to-contribution when employees move to new teams or take on hybrid responsibilities. - Improve internal mobility rates and reduce hiring ramp costs. - Create repeatable handoff artifacts and templates that preserve institutional knowledge. Program variants - Short Fellowship (6 weeks): Focused learning sprint with one well-scoped deliverable. Best for tooling, docs, or experiment-driven work. - Standard Fellowship (9 weeks): Balanced discovery + delivery rhythm; includes a small end-to-end feature or migration task. - Deep Fellowship (12 weeks): For complex integrations, security/compliance projects, or multi-team migration planning. Eligibility and nomination - Who can apply: Regular ICs (L2–L5), staff-level engineers with manager consent, product managers, and member-of-staff customer success leads. - Manager approval: A written manager sign-off is required and must include a statement of support and a continuity plan for the fellow's home responsibilities. - Skill fit: Fellowship proposals must map to at least two measurable learning objectives and one deliverable for the host team. - Frequency: An individual may participate in the RPF up to twice in any 24-month period; exceptions require director-level approval. Key roles and responsibilities - Fellow (participant) - Own learning objectives, attend host team ceremonies, and deliver the agreed project artifact. - Maintain weekly updates to the home manager and host lead. - Home manager - Provide approval, maintain backfill plan (short-term coverage or task reprioritization), and maintain performance context. - Host lead - Assign a mentor, define the scope, and ensure access to systems and documentation. - Mentor (primary contact on the host team) - Provide day-to-day guidance, onboarding to codebase and tooling, and review deliverables. - People Ops (program owner) - Coordinate nominations, maintain fellowship schedule, run kickoff and wrap ceremonies, and keep program metrics. Selection process and timeline 1. Proposal submission (Week -3 to -2): Fellow or manager submits a 1-page proposal: goals, proposed host team, duration, and success criteria. 2. Triage (Week -2): People Ops validates eligibility and confirms host team capacity. 3. Approvals (Week -2 to -1): Home manager and host lead sign the rotation agreement. 4. Kickoff (Day 0): Program kickoff with People Ops, host mentor, fellow, and home manager. Agree on communication cadence, tooling access, and handoff milestones. 5. Midpoint check-in (Week 3–6): Formal review between the fellow, mentor, and home manager to adjust scope if needed. 6. Wrap & knowledge transfer (Final week): Document handoff, close tickets, and present outcomes at a cross-team demo. Rotation agreement template (1-page) - Title: [Fellow name] — [Host team] — [Duration] - Learning objectives: • Objective 1 • Objective 2 - Deliverable(s): • Artifact A (link) • Artifact B (link) - Duration and schedule: [start date] — [end date], expected weekly hours committed to host - Success criteria: 3 measurable acceptance checks - Approvals: Home manager | Host lead | People Ops Access and tooling checklist (example table) | Category | Items | Responsible | Target complete | |---------|-------|-------------|----------------| | Codebase | Repo access (read/write), CI runner tokens | Host lead | Day 2 | | Jira | Project write access, issue templates | Host lead | Day 2 | | Slack | Host team channel + #rpf-fellows | People Ops | Day 1 | | Cloud / Infra | Role-based access, test environment | Host lead + Security | Day 3 | | Analytics | Dashboard viewers, query access | Host lead | Day 4 | Onboarding & first-week cadence - Day 0: Kickoff meeting, rotation agreement sign-off, access checklist start. - Day 1–2: Codebase walkthrough, repo onboarding, run a local dev build, join host team standup and planning. - Day 3–5: Shadow mentor on core workflows, pick up first small task, weekly 1:1 scheduled with home manager and mentor. Performance management and compensation - The fellow remains on their home manager's org and payroll; there is no compensation change for standard rotations. - Performance feedback for the rotation is fed into the fellow's regular performance cycle by the home manager; the host lead provides a written rotation evaluation for the fellow's file. - Promotions and role changes resulting from the rotation are handled through standard promotion/transfer processes and require manager/director approval. Reporting, success metrics, and program KPIs People Ops will track and publish the following quarterly: - Fellowship count and completion rate (target completion >= 90%). - Average time to first meaningful contribution on host team (target <= 3 weeks for 6–9 week rotations). - Internal mobility conversion: percent of fellows who transfer roles within 12 months (target 18%+). - Fellow satisfaction (post-fellow NPS; target >= 8/10). - Document artifact quality: percent of handoffs with complete docs and runbooks (target >= 95%). Knowledge capture and handoff requirements - Every fellowship must close with a Confluence handoff page located under: /confluence/teams/[host-team]/rpf-handoffs/[fellow-name]-YYYYMMDD. - Required artifacts: - Architecture decision notes or design doc - Runbooks for anything operated in production - Test plan and known failure modes - A clear list of tickets left open and who will own them post-rotation Budgeting and perks - People Ops maintains a small rotation budget for cross-team learning. Typical reimbursable items include conference passes (pre-approved), short dedicated training, and workspace ergonomics for a remote fellow. - Fellows are eligible for a one-time learning stipend (up to $800) to cover books, courses, or small equipment purchases, pending manager sign-off. - Hosts can request a temporary headcount shadow (up to 2 weeks) for critical backfill; approvals routed through People Ops. Risk management and security - Sensitive projects (PII, audited) require a security review prior to approval. Host lead must list data accesses and sign off with Security. - If a rotation overlaps scheduled on-call windows, explicit contingency coverage must be documented before Day 0. - Hosts are responsible for ensuring fellows follow the host team's incident escalation and access policies. Wrap ceremony and knowledge sharing - All completed fellowships are celebrated in the RPF wrap ceremony (monthly hybrid town hall) where fellows present a 10-minute demo and learning recap. - Post-fellow writeups are published to a shared RPF Confluence space and linked to the home manager's performance notes. Measurement and continuous improvement - People Ops will run bi-annual retrospectives with host leads and a representative set of fellows to iterate on the program. - The RPF handbook will be updated annually or following significant process changes. FAQs - Q: Can fellows be on partial rotations (e.g., 50% time)? - A: Yes, with explicit manager and host lead approval; these are considered "embedded rotations" and require a more detailed continuity plan. - Q: Does the fellow keep their equity vesting schedule? - A: Yes, compensation and equity schedules are unchanged. - Q: Who owns the final deliverable? - A: The host team owns the deliverable post-handoff unless otherwise negotiated in the rotation agreement. Related links and templates - Rotation agreement template: /confluence/templates/rpf-agreement - Confluence handoff template: /confluence/templates/rpf-handoff - People Ops program calendar: /confluence/people-ops/rpf-schedule Stakeholders and escalation - Program owner: People Ops (Primary contact: people-ops@redwood.ai) - Escalations: Home manager -> Host lead -> Director of People Ops - Security review: Security (security@redwood.ai) for regulated projects Revision history - 2028-02-15: Version 1.0 — initial published manual (People Ops author) - 2028-03-01: Version 1.1 — clarified embedded rotation policy and added stipend details

top_candidates.title: sam: Hey team — quick sync: we have a customer on Dedicated who hit capacity and got routed to Hosted, but the model variant on Hosted was a smaller quantized variant and the outputs were subtly different. Customer flagged it as a data-sensitivity concern. How should we handle routing when variant compatibility isn't exact? :thinking: elaine: Ugh. Was that routed by the current "tiered-fallback" policy? I thought Dedicated tenants could opt-out of spillover to Hosted. sam: They did not opt-out. Default is allow_spillover = true for mid-tier. They expected functional parity though. ravi: Two quick axes: (1) policy surface (console + API) vs org defaults, (2) telemetry/traceability so we can show customers what variant served them. We should fail closed if strict_isolation=true and otherwise attach routing_reason. alex: +1 on routing_reason. We also need a compatibility matrix check at routing time: if hosted variant model.arch != dedicated.model.arch or quant != quant we should either (a) refuse, (b) degrade gracefully with explicit header, or (c) fall back to a compatible hosted variant. Which is preferred? maria: For regulated customers, default should be refuse (reject) unless they explicitly allow variant-relaxed fallback. For mid-market, maybe allow but mark in console and send audit event. sam: Implementation idea: add a pre-routing hook that emits an event: {tenant, requested_variant, candidate_variant, compatibility_score, routing_decision}. Console shows per-request the last routing_decision and a link to the eval set used. Example event payload we could emit: { "tenant_id": "acct_ABC", "requested_model": "redwood/dedicated-xl-v2", "candidate_model": "redwood/hosted-xlq-quant", "compatibility_score": 0.72, "routing_decision": "spillover_with_variant_warning" } ravi: We should keep the schema minimal but searchable in logs. Suggest fields: routing_reason, variant_delta (enum: arch_mismatch, quant_diff, seq_len_limit), compatibility_score, override_flag. elaine: UX question: where does the customer configure this? Console toggle per-tenant + API field per-request? We need both. Per-request override should be rate-limited and audited. alex: Console affordance: add a toggle "Allow variant-relaxed spillover" (off by default for enterprise). Also surface last N routed requests with their routing_reason and compatibility_score. Add a big red badge when any routed request had variant_delta != none. maria: Also need a billing note: if the hosted variant has different perf/cost, we should surface potential cost delta on console and in invoice events. ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolled out routing_reason field to staging at 2130001100. Watch logs: /staging/routing/events sam: Nice. Edge-case: what if dedicated capacity is available but slow; should we prefer lower latency hosted variant over a busy dedicated? We currently route by priority: dedicated > hosted, but we could route by expected tail latency vs SLO. ravi: We can compute expected_latency = queue_time + p95_inference for variant. Add a policy expression: route_if(expected_latency(hosted) < expected_latency(dedicated) * 0.9 AND compatibility_score >= 0.9). That lets us choose hosted for latency-sensitive bursts. elaine: That policy sounds powerful but complex. Need to expose a safe default and a "policy editor" for advanced teams. Also need simulation UI: show hypothetical routing outcomes for last 24h. alex: Telemetry: add a tag on token-level logs: "served_variant" and "requested_variant", plus a trace_id linking request->fallback decision path. This makes debugging customer-reported regressions possible. maria: Ops-wise, we must ensure hosted variants serving PII-sensitive tenants are not used unless allowed. Add check: tenant_data_classification != pii OR allow_relaxed_spillover = true. sam: Action items: - [ ] add routing_reason, variant_delta, compatibility_score to routing events (ravi+alex) - [ ] console toggle and history UI (elaine+maria) - [ ] per-request API override + audit (alex) - [ ] default policy change for enterprise tenants to refuse (sam) - [ ] billing exposure for variant cost delta (maria) - [ ] add simulation in Console for policy changes (elaine) ravi: I'll draft the event schema tonight and post here. Also adding a small proposal for the compatibility_score heuristic: match on architecture, tokenizer, quantization, and output-stability evals. sam: Thanks. Let's keep default behavior conservative: reject for high-sensitivity customers, otherwise allow with warning and strong telemetry. :thumbsup: ops-bot: note: follow-up doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/routing/variant-fallback-proposal (draft)

top_candidates.title: ana: quick thought — proposal to relax embeddings endpoint so clients can send mixed-dim arrays if they opt in via header. router would split into uniform sub-batches and route per-model. avoids a lot of 413 churn for multi-model clients. sam: how do we bill/charge for splits? we'd need predictable quota semantics or we'll get support tickets. ana: plan: bill per original item using the target model's unit price. for splitter-generated child requests we emit telemetry linking child -> parent ID so usage and billing are reconciled server-side. clients still see single response. jordan: worry: splitting adds overhead and hurts batching efficiency. our load tests for runtime splitter showed ~3% 95p token latency increase on p3-like nodes. meera: console/telemetry needs: show split_rate, avg_splits_per_request, and per-split latency histogram. also surface percentage of requests that had partial failures. we should add a column in per-route table: "split enabled". ana: implementation notes: ``` Header: X-Embeddings-Allow-Split: true Payload: { "inputs": [[...],[...]], "model": "embed-large" } Router: if mixed dims -> create child reqs grouped by dims -> forward Response: 200 + { "results": [...], "split_info": { "children": 3, "partial_failures": [] } } ``` sam: partial failures — do we return 207 Multi-Status or always 200 with per-item status? returning 207 breaks a lot of SDKs. meera: prefer 200 with per-item status array. then console can show failure rate. SDKs parse it as normal. jordan: canary suggestion: feature flag default-off for hosted; enable for dedicated customers by config first. tag telemetry: split_feature=canary-<id>. rollout only after we have split-aware batching in runtime. infra-bot: load-test comment: "splitter + per-child routing" increased CPU on router by 8% and added 0.5ms to median request path in our 50k req/s test. (perf-run id: perf/2026-03-12/43) sam: need billing docs change: if child fails we still charge for successful children. if parent-level timeout occurs before children finish we prorate recorded tokens. I'll draft language. meera: UX: add a small indicator on route details: "split enabled (canary)" and a histogram for split_count; add alert if split_rate > 10% and 95p latency regresses > 2x compared to baseline. jordan: I'll prototype router split + telemetry events this week. can follow this cf-branch: feature/embed-splitter. I'll post PR with perf numbers. ana: action items: jordan prototype, meera console metrics + alert rules, sam billing blurb, i'll write RFC and include traffic model + SLO targets. :thumbsup: sam: :thumbsup: thanks. can we also log a sample of original payloads that trigger split for 24h for debugging? redaction required. ana: yes — sample at 0.1% with PII redaction. will include in RFC. meera: ok, i'm adding telemetry fields: ["parent_request_id","child_request_ids","split_count","split_reason","split_enabled_flag"], will send schema. jordan: noted. I'll tag all child requests with parent_request_id and split_version. ana: cool. I'll open the RFC tomorrow and cc infra/product. end.

elaine_pm: Quick sync 011: EU enterprise wants an A/B experiment for the new routing policy but insists: no cross-border logs, and automatic user-facing fallback if latency > 300ms p95 for 3m. How do we design the rollout?

luis_sre: thresholds proposal: if p95 > 300ms for 3m -> SOFT_DEGRADE; if p95 stays > 350ms or error-rate > 2% for 5m -> HARD_FALLBACK. automated rollback if user-visible errors > 5% or user complaints flagged via support integration.

top_candidates.title: Marta: Heads up — thinking about adding small routing/quota + telemetry annotations to saved views. Idea: saved views carry a lightweight "hints" section with sampling, preferred route, and quota estimate. Wanted reactions before I spin up an API PR. Jordan: ++ need this for rollout gating. If a saved view can say 'sample_rate: 5%' we can auto-apply higher-fidelity telemetry during experiments without manual toggles. Matt: UX thought — compact badge on saved view card: 'Q:5% | S:10k' or 'route: r196'. Click -> preview implications modal. Keep main list uncluttered. Lee: API note — we'd need to extend the savedquery schema. Two approaches: embed metadata in existing object or have a separate viewHints resource. I lean separate to avoid breaking clients. Simone: Telemetry caveat — sample rate is not monolithic. Traces vs token-level vs eval sampling all differ. We need clear keying. Marta: Good point. Proposal (simple): keys: routing_hint (route_id), quota_est (tokens_per_min), telemetry_sample:{type:rate}. Example: ```{ "routing_hint":"route-196", "quota_est":"1200tpm", "telemetry_sample":{ "trace":"1%", "eval":"10%" } }``` Lee: Implementation nit — our persisted schema prefers flat columns. Nested telemetry_sample will mean special parsing. I suggest flattened keys like telemetry_trace_sample and telemetry_eval_sample. Jordan: For rollouts we also want an optional fallback_route policy so saved views can define an ordered routing preference when capacity is constrained. Matt: Also worth showing a quick cost-estimate on hover computed from model profile + quota_est so product teams can see currency impact before they push. Marta: Open question: permissioning. Who can add routing_hint? Org admins only? Team owners? This could become a way to steer traffic. Simone: Policy: only view owners + org admins can set routing_hint. Others can save copies but hints are stripped unless they have rights. Lee: API contract draft: PATCH /savedviews/:id with body keys under view_hints.*. We'll implement migration and feature-flag it. Marta: I'll write an RFC with UI mocks + API sketch. TL;DR: saved views get optional hints for routing/quota/telemetry; UI badges + preview; separate hints endpoint; RBAC control. Jordan: Sounds good. Can we gate behind flag feature.saved_view_hints so we can dogfood? ops-bot: feature flag created: feature.saved_view_hints for org=redwood-beta Matt: :thumbsup: Simone: One more — telemetry sampling overrides must emit audit logs with who/when/which-view so we can tie experiments to data quality changes. Lee: Noted — will add audit entries on hint mutations. Marta: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC link once it's up. Short-term action: Jordan + Lee sync on API/console mockups tomorrow. Jordan: I'll pick this up tomorrow morning, adding API sketch to the RFC.

top_candidates.title:
elaine_pm: Quick sync 011: EU enterprise wants an A/B experiment for the new routing policy but insists: no cross-border logs, and automatic user-facing fallback if latency > 300ms p95 for 3m. How do we design the rollout?

mike_research: key asks: 1) per-tenant/region A/B assignment, 2) telemetry bounded to EU KMS, 3) deterministic opt-in/opt-out for customers.

nora_eng: engineering constraints: we have per-tenant flags and region routing already. A/B split can be done via the routing layer but need deterministic hashing + sticky assignment. We should avoid global KV for assignments to keep EU data local.
luis_sre: ops concerns: automatic user-visible fallback for latency spikes is risky unless we have a cascading rollback plan. propose two-tier fallback: soft degrade (route to cheaper model variant) then hard fallback (route to legacy routing) if soft degrade doesn't recover in 5m.
elaine_pm: agree two-tier fallback is sensible. customers prefer immediate visible fallback vs silent regressions. we should include customer-facing banner in UI when fallback happens.
mike_research: for A/B metrics: primary KPI = latency p95 and error rate, secondary = model quality delta (via sample evaluation hooks). Need test harness to sample outputs and run gold prompts.
nora_eng: implementation sketch: 1) A/B assignment in-region using tenant_id % 100 < X. 2) telemetry aggregated by EU-only collectors -> KMS in EU. 3) gating service evaluates sliding windows of metrics and emits actions: NOOP / SOFT_DEGRADE / HARD_FALLBACK / ROLLBACK.
luis_sre: thresholds proposal: if p95 > 300ms for 3m -> SOFT_DEGRADE; if p95 stays > 350ms or error-rate > 2% for 5m -> HARD_FALLBACK. automated rollback if user-visible errors > 5% or user complaints flagged via support integration.
elaine_pm: regulatory check: legal insists the audit log for experiments be stored in EU for EU customers. prodops, can we automate that?
nora_eng: yes we can write experiment events to EU-only logging pipeline when tenant.region == "EU". small change in event producer, ETA 1 sprint.
prodops-bot: Reminder: create calendar block for "EU A/B bake (prod)" and include oncall; add runbook link. (automated)
mike_research: can we do a shadow run first? send 100% traffic in shadow to new routing and collect latency/quality without impacting users. then flip % of traffic in small increments: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> full. each step gated by metric windows.
luis_sre: agree on shadowing first. Also request: add a canary host pool that isolates model variant under test to avoid cache contamination.
elaine_pm: decision checklist for this thread: 1) require EU-local telemetry+audit for EU tenants, 2) shadow test then phased %-ramp with deterministic in-region assignment, 3) two-tier fallback (soft degrade to cheaper variant, then hard fallback to legacy), 4) automated gating + rollback thresholds as proposed. any objections?
nora_eng: no objections. will draft spec: routing-hash details, event tagging, canary pool config.
mike_research: no objections. I'll prepare evaluation prompt set and acceptance criteria for quality delta.
luis_sre: no objections. I'll write the rollback runbook and thresholds into SRE playbooks.
elaine_pm: next steps: nora to open spec PR and link canary config; mike to upload eval suite; luis to add runbook and pager triggers. weekly check-in Thurs 10:30.
prodops-bot: Action items created: #4821 spec PR, #4822 eval suite, #4823 rollback runbook. (automated)
elaine_pm: thanks team. I'll notify EU customer and align timelines.

top_candidates.title: SRE-bot: INCIDENT CREATED - routing-service tail latency surge detected, streaming stalls and increased 5xxs. paging: @maria (oncall). Incident ID INC-4299 Maria (oncall): ack. seeing p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 1.3s, streaming stall percentage ~4.2%. multiple customers reporting streaming interruptions (NimbusData, PaperclipAI). grabbing logs. Akshay: initial glance at routing weight tables shows a suspicious concentration. rolling-affinity v2 was promoted yesterday. I see many micro-weights assigned which might be colliding in the selector. Jess: router logs show repeated stream resets to the same shard id. sample lines: ``` [router] 2026-03-15T05:02:11Z POST /v1/stream id=cid-99 upstream=shard-42 status=200 stream-reset=1 latency_ms=1389 [model-proxy] 2026-03-15T05:02:11Z shard-42 queue=410 active=420 ``` This looks like queue buildup on shard-42. Carter (night-oncall): I'm in. which regions most impacted? Akshay: us-west-2 and eu-central show disproportionate hit-rate to shard-42 and shard-7. weight snapshot (excerpt): ``` shard-42: 0.00009 shard-7: 0.00010 shard-3: 0.99981 ``` Selector normalization uses a float->int floor which seems to bias mapping for certain prefixes; when many tiny weights exist, hashing modulo maps them to same low-id bucket. I can reproduce locally. Maria (oncall): mitigation options: (A) immediate rollback of rolling-affinity v2 to v1 (global), (B) apply emergency weight floor config (treat weights < 0.001 as 0) and re-normalize, (C) route-streams to bypass pool (force round-robin) for affected routes. Which gives fastest relief? Jess: canary rollback might take longer. emergency config floor is quickest. Ops-Runner can push config fast. Ops-Runner: I can push a config patch in ~4 mins. ready on go. Akshay: I'll assemble the config patch now — minimal change: treat tiny weights as zero and re-normalize across remaining shards. SRE-bot: config-push started (cfg-98890) by Akshay. expect propagation ~40-50s per zone. Maria (oncall): pushing Ops-Runner to scale streaming pool preemptively +2 replicas while patch propagates. Ops-Runner: scaling streaming-pool from 10 -> 12. Jess: canary nodes show p99 drop from ~1.3s -> 700ms. queue lengths on shard-42 drop from 410 -> 90. Good sign. SRE-bot: config-push rolled to 60% routers. Maria (oncall): global p95 now 210ms, p99 ~710ms, streaming stalls ~1.1%. improvement but still above SLO. Carter, take ownership for steady-state monitoring. I'll handoff. Carter (night-oncall): taking it. summary: emergency weight-floor applied; observe p99 and streaming stalls for 30m. run `redis-cli -h routing-store HGETALL weights:affinity:v2` and identify values < 0.001. run `scripts/hotmap.sh --window=10m` to produce hotkey map. Carter (night-oncall): hotmap shows shard-42 receiving ~58% of certain prefix hashes. Akshay: root cause hypothesis: selector normalization rounding bug causes many tiny weights to be represented similarly in the integer hashing domain, leading to mapping collisions and hot partitions. Repro steps and unit test added. Jess: action: open rollback PR if config patch doesn't finish improving within 15m. Also capture log buffer for 10m window for postmortem. Olivia (pm): customer impact: NimbusData claims ~12% sessions affected; we should notify customers on affected list and offer mitigation timeline. prepping comms. Maria (oncall): assign tasks: @Akshay to open PR with selector fix + tests, @Jess to run stress tests against fixed selector in staging, @Carter to draft incident notification and post to #incidents-notify, @Ops-Runner to keep scaling plan ready. Akshay: created PR https://git.company/repo/pulls/1430 with unit tests and changelog. requesting expedited review. will also add configuration assertion to reject configs with >30% total weight in micro-weight shards. SRE-bot: EVENT: mitigation_applied by Akshay at 2765439999. Carter (night-oncall): current metrics: 30m rolling p99 ~ 640ms, p95 205ms, streaming stalls 0.9%. Still above p99 SLO of 500ms. will monitor for 1h then re-evaluate rollback. Maria (oncall): leaving pager. Carter you're primary. escalate to oncall lead if p99 > 800ms for 15m. Carter (night-oncall): ack. posting interim incident note to #incidents-notify in 8m. Jess: note for postmortem: include timeline of config propagation across regions (we saw ~50s lag per zone) which impacted how fast canary improvement translated to global SLOs. Olivia (pm): scheduling follow-up with Support & Solutions at 09:00 UTC tomorrow to coordinate customer outreach. Akshay: additional temporary measure: add selector defensive code to treat weights <0.0005 as 0 and add telemetry to flag when >5% of config entries are micro-weights. will include in PR. Ops-Runner: scaled streaming pool +2 completed. SRE-bot: Pager cleared by Maria. Carter (night-oncall): marking incident mitigated for now. will keep monitoring and prepare postmortem draft. adding backlog items: full rollback exercise, more robust selector tests, telemetry for micro-weight configs. Maria (oncall): great work team. keep an eye on customer tickets and confirm any required credits or remediation.

top_candidates.title: maya: Heads up — after we pushed the 535.86 driver + CUDA 12.2 roll last night, we've got a regression: NVLink topology isn't being detected on mixed A100 nodes. NCCL falls back to SHM -> SOCKET for most peer transfers, huge perf hit. leo: which cluster/region? maya: prod-gpu-eu, also seeing on staging-us-west. Only on racks that have a mix of kernel versions (5.15.x + 6.1.x) and some older A100-SXM nodes. taylor: any logs or nccl topo dump? short snips are fine. maya: paste: ``` $ nvidia-smi topo --matrix GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 CPU GPU0 X NV PHB SYS GPU1 NV X PHB SYS GPU2 PHB PHB X SYS ``` but nccl shows: ``` NCCL INFO Topo: NVLINK not usable between 0 and 1 (p2p query failed) NCCL WARN All-to-all using SOCKET fallback for peer 0-1 NCCL INFO SHM disabled (IPC failure) ``` indra: SHM disabled often due to IPC namespace or missing /dev/shm mount in container. Are these in k8s pods with ipcMode? any change in runtime flags? maya: pods are default, we didn't change --ipc. Container runtime didn't update, only driver and kernel modules. dmesg on one node: ``` [ 428.123456] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: P2P peer lookup failed, peer 0000:3a:00.0 [ 428.123460] nvidia-mig: failed to query P2P capability ``` jun: Could be the kernel driver ABI mismatch — mixing dkms-built modules with packaged driver? Which package mechanism did we use for 535? rpm or runfile? maya: runfile installer (we used for faster rollout). Some older nodes still had kernel module from 525 and we forced install but didn't rebuild DKMS properly. leo: that explains P2P failures. If module symbols mismatch, NVLink P2P ioctl can fail and NCCL disables p2p. Workaround: put affected nodes into maintenance and roll back to 525, or rebuild kernel module via dkms and reboot. taylor: timeline wise, can we isolate by node label and cordon? Also we should avoid full rollback if we can hotfix: rebuild modules and restart kubelet + container runtime to rebind devices. maya: doing a canary: cordoned 2 nodes in prod-gpu-eu and initiated dkms rebuild + reboot. I'll report perf after. ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0783 - "NVLink/NCCL P2P regressions after 535 driver rollout". Pager on-call: leo, taylor. indra: another mitigation: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to force consistent path (explicit SOCKET) while we fix drivers — avoids random mixed behavior, but costs throughput. Also NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1 if IPC is flaky. jun: note: forcing SOCKET may hurt multi-node perf but keeps correctness; useful temporary flag for training jobs that can't tolerate nondeterministic fallbacks. maya: perf numbers after canary rebuild: peer bandwidth for single-GPU pairs went from 3.2 GB/s (socket fallbacks) back to 72 GB/s when NVLink restored. Good sign. taylor: good. Next steps: - create an automated check during driver rollout: run `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` + `nccl-tests` smoke to validate NVLink/SHM - add DKMS verification in rollout playbook - add node label to identify kernel-driver mismatches maya: I'll open a PR to update the rollout runbook + add a k8s admission job that checks /dev/shm and ipc namespace for GPU pods. leo: also add a step: if module version mismatch detected, mark node drainable and block burst autoscaler from placing new GPU pods. maya: noted. will follow up with timeline and postmortem notes. srebot: Deploy log: driver-rollout-2025-03-22 completed on 2025-03-22T02:13:00Z. 17 nodes patched, 4 nodes reported dkms mismatch. maya: thanks — tagging this thread for postmortem. Any objections to rolling back the remaining 3 mismatched nodes to 525-runfile and re-testing before reapplying 535 via dkms package? taylor: +1. safer and we can automate dkms-based rollout afterwards. leo: please include cost impact estimate in postmortem (retries + slower jobs). I expect ~12% longer training time for affected jobs in EU yesterday. maya: will include. closing the loop when PR/PM posted.

top_candidates.title:
incident-bot: ALERT: autoscaler-oscillation detected in prod (us-east-1). metric: gpu_pool_utilization. spikes -> rapid scale ups/downs causing request failures. paging ryan-oncall and team. incident id: INC-20260315-8423 :rotating_light:
ryan-oncall: got it. i'm oncall. looking at autoscaler metrics now. can someone post recent spike graphs?
erin-sre: pulling logs for the last 30m. seeing repeated scale events: scale_up -> scale_down loop. kube events show NodeJoin/NodeTerminate churn.
mike-rtc: seeing a correlated burst of short-lived batch jobs from a customer integration (internal-job-runner). sending link to logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/trace/abcd1234
kate-csm: FYI, CSM told me a few enterprise customers reported 502/503s around 09:42-09:58. one raised a support ticket (SUP-5492).
dmitri-eng: could be autoscaler cooldown too short + pod readiness flapping. what's current autoscaler config?
erin-sre: current config snippet: ```yaml
minReplicas: 2
maxReplicas: 50
scaleUpPolicy: immediate
scaleDownCooldown: 30s
scaleUpCooldown: 10s
```
that scaleDownCooldown is probably too aggressive for GPU nodes.
ryan-oncall: immediate mitigation attempt: disabling aggressive scaleDown for the pool and forcing stable size to 12 while we investigate. running: `redwood-cli pool set --name gpu-us-east-1 --target 12`
ops-bot: ACTION: pool gpu-us-east-1 target set to 12 by ryan-oncall. previous target 6.
sarah-qa: after scaling target to 12, error rate dropped to baseline ~1.2% within 3 minutes. looks like mitigation worked. :thumbsup:
kate-csm: passing update to affected customers, telling them we mitigated and investigating root cause.
jasmin-ops: planning post-incident review. prefer a short postmortem meeting today. who can join? propose 16:00 UTC.
dmitri-eng: I can join. want to review autoscaler tuning, job throttling, and add hard limits on short batch bursts.
erin-sre: will prepare timeline + extracted logs.
ryan-oncall: assign follow-ups here. immediate action items in-thread: 1) revert scaleDownCooldown to safer value and add min cooldown 5m for GPU pools (owner: erin-sre) 2) add request throttling to internal-job-runner to smooth bursts (owner: dmitri-eng) 3) create alert that detects >3 scale events in 10m for same pool (owner: mike-rtc) 4) customer comms recap (owner: kate-csm) 5) add canary for autoscaler config changes (owner: jasmin-ops)
erin-sre: creating ticket INFRA-2741 with details and immediate config change notes. linking runbook: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/autoscaler-runbook
mike-rtc: I will add the "oscillation" alert rule and a dashboard panel showing scale events per minute.
ops-bot: TASK CREATED: INFRA-2741 (autoscaler cooldown and remediation) assigned to erin-sre.
jasmin-ops: scheduled postmortem meeting 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC. invite sent to participants and stakeholders. meeting link: https://meet.internal/redwood/pm-INC-20260315-8423
dmitri-eng: quick note — internal-job-runner had a recent deployment that changed retry policy; rolling back might reduce the burst. I'll coordinate with platform team.
kate-csm: customer updates sent. two customers requested SLA credit evaluation; capturing in SUP-5492.
erin-sre: after mitigation, adding a short-term guard in autoscaler logic: disallow scaleDown if last scaleUp < 300s. pushing patch to staging and will roll to prod after smoke. snippet: ```go
if now.Sub(lastScaleUp) < 5*time.Minute {
 skipScaleDown()
}
```
ryan-oncall: nice. once patch is live, let's monitor for 24h. set a follow-up check in status board.
sarah-qa: will run synthetic traffic tests to ensure we don't regress (target windows: 10m bursts and steady).
jasmin-ops: postmortem owners: infra -> erin-sre (write prose + timeline), eng -> dmitri-eng (root cause analysis + mitigation), devex -> mike-rtc (alerts + dashboards), support -> kate-csm (customer comms). deadline for draft: 2026-03-18 EOD.
erin-sre: draft created at https://confluence.redwood/postmortems/INC-20260315-8423-draft. linking logs and timeline.
dmitri-eng: created remediation epic: EPIC-1210 (autoscaler hardening). will break into tasks and add estimated ETA.
ops-bot: REMINDER: postmortem draft due 2026-03-18.
ryan-oncall: final note — we should add autoscaler simulation tests in CI to catch oscillation patterns before prod. filing infra task.
jasmine-ops: (typo) jasmin-ops: moving thread to follow-up and closing active paging; will reopen if new problems. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-20260315-8423 status: mitigated — impact contained. severity: Sev2. closing page.
jasmin-ops: postmortem meeting notes will be appended to the confluence draft and action items tracked in EPIC-1210. thanks everyone for quick response.
ryan-oncall: handing off to erin-sre for follow-ups. I'm out of rotation.
erin-sre: ack. taking ownership of follow-ups. will post updates in INFRA-2741 as tasks progress.

Symptoms: sudden spike in NCCL communicator errors and multi-GPU hangs, repeated container restarts on nodes gpu-12,gpu-13,gpu-17. Error rate > 20% for /v1/generate on model-xlarge-8way. I want the first glimpse of the NCCL stack. ml_infra_lee: Pasting trimmed log from pod inference-runtime-xyz (rank 2): ``` [2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL WARN Unhandled cuda error, aborting [2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL ERROR ncclCommAbort called, communicator invalid [2026-03-15 02:45:21] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error' runtime_error: cudaLaunchKernel failed: out of resources at /workspace/runtime/collective/comm.c:412 at /usr/local/bin/inference-runtime ``` We're also seeing container restarts (`CrashLoopBackOff`) and occasional OOMs on the GPU when sequence length spikes. eng_omar: Likely bad interaction between kernel scheduling and tensor parallel communicator. Could be a race on communicator teardown when a pod gets preempted. Quick mitigation: reduce tensor-parallel degree for active model-route and shift traffic to a smaller single-gpu variant. I'll prepare route change if SRE gives go. sre_jamie: Immediate mitigation plan (proposed): 1) Temporarily mark the 3 problematic nodes unschedulable (cordon) to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 gpu-13 gpu-17`. 2) Drain the failing pods and restart the runtime on healthy nodes: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl delete pod -l app=inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-12` for each. 3) Apply fallback routing: shift 40% of traffic for model-xlarge-8way to model-xlarge-1gpu (lower throughput, safe single-gpu path). 4) If restarts persist, scale model instances down to TP_SIZE=1/PP_SIZE=1 for the route and restart the deployment. ml_infra_lee: Executed step 1 & 2 on gpu-12 and gpu-13. Logs show one node had `nvidia-driver` OOM trace and GPU driver process got killed. I cordoned gpu-17 but didn't drain yet (still serving). Sample command I ran: ``` kubectl cordon gpu-12 kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-xyz-2 ``` cs_tara: Any idea which customers hit 5xxs? AcmeFinance just flagged errors in prod. Need ETA to share with them. ml_infra_lee: From metrics: AcmeFinance and BetaRetail were the top two that hit elevated 5xx counts. Total user-facing error rate peaked ~18% on the route. After cordon+drain the error rate dropped to ~6% but still above baseline. eng_omar: I'm ready to change routing. If SRE confirms the partial reroute, I'll do a canary 20% -> 80% to test stability. sre_jamie: Do it. eng_omar make it 25/75 for 10 minutes, watch latency and error stream. deploy-bot: Routing update started by eng_omar: model-xlarge-8way -> 25% traffic to model-xlarge-1gpu. Rollout id: r-20260315-1759 ml_infra_lee: After routing shift we saw error rate go to ~2-3% but latency increased on the single-gpu path as expected. No more NCCL communicator aborts on nodes still serving. Meanwhile, pod restarts have stopped on gpu-12 and gpu-13. ops_maya: I suggest we also enable NCCL debugging envs on a staging replica to capture more info: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL`. Also consider setting `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` briefly to rule out p2p prob. sre_jamie: Good call. But don't flood prod logs. Run debug on a single canary pod in a non-customer shard. ml_infra_lee: Created a debug deployment `inference-debug-canary` with NCCL_DEBUG enabled and TP/PP set to same as prod. Collecting traces now. sre_jamie: Next steps for live mitigation: keep nodes cordoned, maintain 25/75 routing split, finish draining gpu-17 if safe, and run a controlled rollout with TP_SIZE=1 for model-xlarge across the cluster if we see reoccurrence. Also open a ticket for post-incident capacity adjustments. cs_tara: Sending a short customer update: "We're investigating elevated errors on model-xlarge; traffic has been partially rerouted to a stable variant and we're working on node restarts. ETA 1h for remediation" — ok to send? sre_jamie: OK to send. Add note that some customers may see higher latency. pagerduty: On-call handoff: sre_jamie -> ops_maya at 03:15 UTC. Handoff acknowledged. PagerDuty note: continue mitigation, collect debug logs, and escalate to HW vendor if driver kills persist. ops_maya: Took over. Running NVIDIA diagnostics on gpu-17 now (`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CEC,PERSISTENCE`). One node shows ECC corrected errors increasing. ml_infra_lee: ECC counts rising on gpu-17, and dmesg shows multiple `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` entries. I queued a maintenance for that host with infra: HOST-REPLACE-178. eng_omar: Given suspected hardware instability, we should automate fallback routing for high-latency/5xx spikes in future: if error-rate > 5% for 2m, automatically shift 50% traffic to single-gpu variant. Filing an RFC after mitigation. sre_jamie: Agreed. For now: drained gpu-17 and replaced 2 pods onto healthy nodes. Error rate back to baseline ~0.8%. top_candidates.title: incident-bot: [P1] Canary latency spike detected in canary-west-2-a. 95th/99th token latencies > 600ms vs baseline 120ms. rate of affected requests ~12% over last 5m. alert-rule: canary-tail-latency-crossed. triggered_at=2005004321 Sara (oncall): Paging. I’m on it. grabbing traces and will triage. Alex (eng-runtime): I’m looking at recent deploys — there was a small scheduler change merged in the last deploy (commit 1a2f3b4) that touched worker-affinity and batching heuristics. Rolling back as a safety if we confirm. Marta (eng-sre): Confirmed canary pool nodes showing context-switch bursts and CPU steal on a subset of pods. Looks correlated to the new scheduler flags. Raj (eng-platform): Can we flip the feature flag for the scheduler to the previous behavior? flag: scheduler_v2_enabled (canary). Samir (cs): Heads-up: we’ve seen ~6 customer 500s tied to long tails in the past 10m, customers A/B. No major page for SLOs yet but CS is tracking. Sara (oncall): @Raj please kill the flag for canary. If we need faster: revert the single commit. Which is safer? Raj (eng-platform): Killing the flag now: /feature-toggle set scheduler_v2_enabled=false --env=canary-west-2-a --user=raj deploy-bot: feature-toggle scheduler_v2_enabled false applied to canary-west-2-a by raj at 2005004402. 8/10 canary pods updated. Alex (eng-runtime): After the flag flip some nodes dropped latency quickly, but 2 pods still showing high tail. digging into kernel config and container runtime. Marta (eng-sre): Rolling log snippet: ``` [2005004415] worker[7] batch_loop: scheduling delay=420ms, cpu_wait=380ms [2005004420] worker[3] batch_loop: scheduling delay=610ms, cpu_wait=590ms ``` Sara (oncall): Can we cordon and restart the two affected pods? If they’re stuck in a bad state a restart will be faster than a full revert. Alex (eng-runtime): Agree. Doing `kubectl rollout restart deploy/canary-runtime -l canary=west-2-a --grace-period=0` on the two pods. ETA ~60s. deploy-bot: restart triggered for pod runtime-canary-7 and runtime-canary-3 by Alex at 2005004520. Alex (eng-runtime): Restarts completed. Observability: 99th token latency down to 150ms, 95th ~90ms. Looks like restarts cleared the stuck kernel scheduling. Samir (cs): Customer impact: 14 errors reported in last 30m, most transient. Notified top 2 affected customers and opened tickets. Marta (eng-sre): Root cause hypothesis: scheduler_v2 change increased scheduling jitter under certain host kernel versions (5.15.*) leading to occasional long CPU waits for worker threads. Repro on staging with specific kernel+config. Raj (eng-platform): We should still revert the commit from the previous roll to avoid recurring risk in other regions. I can do a single-commit revert to the canary branch: `git revert --no-edit 1a2f3b4 && git push origin canary` then trigger a patch release. Alex (eng-runtime): Hold on — revert + release will take longer and we already mitigated canary. Can we instead pin the flag off in production rollout pipeline until we validate fixes? That will prevent accidental promotion. Sara (oncall): Agreed. Action items: 1) Raj keep flag off for all rollouts and block promotion from canary. 2) Alex & Marta reproduce on staging and prepare minimal patch (kernel-compat guard) 3) Samir continue customer comms. 4) I’ll update incident timeline and mark P1 watch until next 2h. Raj (eng-platform): Done: promotion blocked in release pipeline at 2005004680. Flag remains false for all envs. Alex (eng-runtime): Started a minimal code patch branch that checks host kernel and disables the changed path when kernel in vulnerable set. Patch is a one-line guard, will open PR now. Alex (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/987 (patch: kernel guard). CI quick checks pass. Marta (eng-sre): Suggest we do a hotfix patch release to canary then run extended soak 1h, then if clean we can merge to main with revert or keep guard. Raj (eng-platform): If patch is single commit we can do a canary hotpatch: `git cherry-pick 9f8e7d6 && deploy --env=canary-west-2-a --tag=hotfix-200500` Sara (oncall): I’ll handoff to the daytime oncall in 20min — @Marta you’ll own watch during business hours? Marta (eng-sre): I can take the handoff and keep an eye on telemetry. Please post quick summary and status. Sara (oncall): Summary: incident triggered by canary scheduler change -> flag killed -> two pods restarted -> latencies returned to near baseline. Promotion pipeline blocked. Hotfix PR opened for kernel-compat guard. Customer impact limited/transient. Marking incident state: mitigated, watch. Samir (cs): I’m updating customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full patch. Thanks team. :thumbsup: incident-bot: Incident state updated to MITIGATED by Sara at 2005004800. Marta (eng-sre): Taking over watch. Will update if any regression in next hour. Sara (oncall): Thanks all, good job.

top_candidates.title: maria: Heads up — starting a controlled rollout for catalog model rwd-titan-1.2. Plan: 10% global traffic canary for 2 hours, then 50% for 4 hours if metrics look good. Fallback ordering will be: rwd-titan-1.2 -> rwd-titan-1.1 (full float) -> rwd-titan-1.1-quant. Pinning: enterprise customers on enterprise-plan will remain pinned to rwd-titan-1.1 unless they opt in. kevin: LGTM. What metrics are we watching for the canary? latency, token cost, and hallucination rate on eval set? maria: yes — p95 latency, tokens/sec cost delta, and the regression test suite on the prompt set (eval-suite/canary_prompts). Alert thresholds in the runbook: p95 +20% or hallucination regression >3% triggers rollback. Also watching error rate and memory OOMs. deploy-bot: deploy-started rwd-catalog-rollout-1753447200 by maria ajay: adding routing config snippet for ops: ``` { "model": "rwd-titan-1.2", "traffic_split": {"canary": 0.10, "stable": 0.90}, "fallback_order": ["rwd-titan-1.2","rwd-titan-1.1","rwd-titan-1.1-quant"], "pinned_customers": {"enterprise-plan": "rwd-titan-1.1"} } ``` sophie: Quick note: rwd-titan-1.2 uses the new attention kernel; infra has GPUs queued on eu-west-1. We should restrict canary to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 only to avoid cross-region anomalies. maria: good catch. updating plan: canary regions = [us-east-1, eu-west-1]. Also enabling KV-prefix caching for repeated chat contexts to reduce per-token cost during canary. deploy-bot: deploy-step complete: routing config applied to catalog service (regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1) — 10% traffic split active kevin: Metrics dashboard link: https://console.redwood/infer/dashboards/canary/1753447200 maria: baseline checks at t+10m: p95 latency +3%, cost per token +1.2%, hallucination delta -0.5% (improvement). No errors. Proceeding to monitor for full 2h. ajay: recording release notes draft: - Model: rwd-titan-1.2 - Changes: attention kernel optimizations; improved summarization on long contexts - Canary: 10% (us-east-1, eu-west-1) - Fallbacks: rwd-titan-1.1 -> rwd-titan-1.1-quant - Pinning: enterprise-plan locked to rwd-titan-1.1 sophie: flag: quant variant rwd-titan-1.1-quant has slightly different tokenizer behavior for emoji sequences — need to watch chat tests. maria: noted. added chat-emoji test to canary eval set. deploy-bot: alert: canary-monitoring detected hallucination_regression = 3.6% at t+1h25m. Auto-escalation triggered. kevin: seeing the same on the eval dashboard. Let's pause rollout. Maria — do you want an immediate rollback to rwd-titan-1.1 for the affected traffic slice? maria: yes — pause traffic expansion and roll back canary to rwd-titan-1.1 for all regions. Keep logs and traces for investigation. We'll open a postmortem if root cause not obvious. deploy-bot: rollback-started rwd-catalog-rollout-1753447200 by maria ajay: command I ran to pin routing back: ``` rls routing set --model rwd-titan-1.1 --scope catalog --traffic 100% ``` deploy-bot: rollback-complete. catalog traffic now pinned to rwd-titan-1.1. Incident ticket created: INC-2025-0427 (assigned to eng-ml). sophie: assigning to @elaine for model quality review and @zack for kernel compatibility. I'll add relevant eval logs. maria: thanks everyone. Action items: - eng-ml: triage hallucination regression on rwd-titan-1.2 (elaine) - infra: check kernel perf/cold starts in eu-west-1 (zack) - product: update release notes to indicate rollback and reason (maria) - devex: hold public catalog announcement until fix kevin: moving this to 'release-blockers' board and adding timeline notes. We'll attempt a narrower patch canary once fixes land. deploy-bot: thread archived: rwd-catalog-rollout-1753447200

Corrective actions: revert the memory-increasing change, add memory guardrails to compile workers, autoscale compile workers based on queue depth, add an alert for compile queue latency and OOMs. Timeline: 23:41 detected -> 23:44 engineers paged -> 23:52 fallback routing applied -> 00:09 baseline restored -> 00:12 fallback rollback completed. ``` Please review and sign-off for customer notification. maria (eng-oncall): Approve, except add a note about follow-up evals to prevent performance regressions under heavy compile traffic. amy (cs): Added that line. Finalizing customer email and posting status page update. I'll send to impacted accounts and include support contact and steps to request SLA credit. allan (sre-manager): :thumbsup: Good job everyone. Post-incident tasks: assign owner for guardrails (dan), run postmortem doc and timeline, confirm SLA impact calc and credit eligibility. I'll schedule the postmortem with stakeholders tomorrow morning.

GPUs at 96-99% on pool dedicated-eu-west-3, memory pressure on two hosts. jamie-support: customer reported failures beginning ~23:10 UTC, marked as "degraded" in ticket #4527. letting them know we're investigating. alex-oncall: quick mitigation proposal: 1) apply tenant-level protective rate limit to acme-prod-01 at 120rps 2) enable short burst autoscale profile (aggressive, +2 nodes, 10m) 3) activate traffic shaping to favor critical routes. objections? maria-ml: +1 to throttling and short aggressive autoscale. KV-cache warmup risk but better than full outages. sam-infra: i can flip the autoscale profile now. running infra toggle: ``` /infra toggle-autoscale --pool dedicated-eu-west-3 --profile aggressive-short --extra-nodes 2 --duration 10m --reason "surge: acme-prod" ``` sam-infra: executed. autoscale event id=96823. new nodes enrolling (3m ETA). alex-oncall: applying tenant rate cap: ``` /admin set-rate-limit --tenant acme-prod-01 --limit 120rps --scope global --ttl 10m --note "protect pool during surge" ``` alex-oncall: rate limit applied. confirm with metrics. maria-ml: metrics: request rate from tenant now capped, overall queue depth starting to fall (75% -> 52%). p95 latency trending down. jamie-support: messaged customer: "We've temporarily throttled your traffic and enabled additional capacity; this should reduce errors while we stabilize. We'll keep you updated." customer replied: "okay, thanks." rene-ops: ensure auto-revert is set and add an explicit rollback checkpoint. don't want accidental long-lived throttles. sam-infra: auto-revert=true on the autoscale toggle; added meta tag rollback_at=+10m. also created alert to notify if queue depth doesn't drop below 40% within 12m. alex-oncall: handing off monitoring to @maria-ml for the next 15m. i'll update runbook with actions taken. statuspage patched (incident: degraded for dedicated-eu-west-3). maria-ml: taking watch. if error-rate doesn't return to baseline after nodes join, escalate to dedicated-sre and consider temporary customer circuit-break (hard deny) for the offending key. jamie-support: customer confirms success rate improved 23:14 UTC: 45%->97% on recent checks. sam-infra: new nodes registered; node util back to ~60-70%. KV cache warmups ongoing but hit-rate improving. autoscale event will auto-revert at 10m. alex-oncall: good. leaving notes: actions = {rate-limit 120rps tenant=acme-prod-01, autoscale aggressive-short +2 nodes duration 10m, statuspage updated, customer notified}. handoff complete. incident-bot: annotation added: autoscale_event=96823, rate_limit_change=rl-5538, ticket=4527. maria-ml: monitoring continues; will post final close when metric window stable. jamie-support: closing customer loop in ticket after final confirmation. alex-oncall: thanks all — if anything regresses ping here or page. maria-ml: final check 23:22 UTC: queue depth 28%, p95 latency back to baseline. marking incident resolved, will file a short postmortem with suggested mitigations (tenant throttles per-policy, improved early-detection for burst imports). incident-bot: incident state -> resolved (resolved_by: maria-ml, duration: 8m).

relations: us-west-2 | asks_cause | What change was applied to reduce the latency spike caused by a KV cache and continuous batching regression on the us-west-2 inference production cluster?

top_candidates.title: incident-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty: continuous-batching errors spike in us-west-2 (sev-2) — several customer sessions timing out, high 502s reported. Auto-create incident channel: #inc-2825554322 maya_oncall: I'm on it, picking up the pager. Observability shows KV cache eviction pressure and paging spikes starting ~10:45 UTC. Latency SLOs breached for some routes. jamie_sre: linking perf dash — https://dash.internal/redwood/contbatch/us-west-2?from=10:30&to=now (watch the max_batch_tokens curve) arjun_runtime: seeing a sudden jump in max_batch_tokens observed per-batch, lots of tiny sequences piling up, causing batching to hit memory limits and triggering aggressive KV cache eviction. tanya_ml: any model-specific regressed? Embeddings or chat? leo_support: early reports from two customers: chat completions stall at token 1 then error 502, some embedding jobs time out after 30s. I've opened cs tickets. maya_oncall: quick customer-impact summary: ~12 tenants impacted intermittently, elevated error rate ~7% on chat-gen, embedding jobs latency 3-5x. No billing anomalies yet. jamie_sre: logs show continuous-batching controller started honoring a new config rollout yesterday — suspected misconfig: max_num_seqs defaulted from 8 -> 64 in prod due to config merge. arjun_runtime: ugh. I remember that PR, the new default was meant for GPU-dedicated hosts but landed in global config. That explains many small sequences packed into huge batches. ines_ops: FYI I just saw paging thrash on host pool gw-9a causing disk swap churn, paging latency skyrocketed. maya_oncall: mitigation plan — short term: revert config to previous safe values for continuous-batching, and throttle batching. Long term: fix config gating. jamie_sre: proposed immediate hotfix: set max_num_seqs=8, max_batch_tokens=2048, request timeout bump to 2s at the batching layer for the affected pool. Canary to 3 hosts first. arjun_runtime: agree. Also temporarily disable prefix KV-sync for the hot pool to reduce KV eviction churn. devex_kate: can we craft a quick runnable patch and rollout playbook so SRE can apply without a full deploy? jamie_sre: patch (will apply via runtime-config service): ``` continuous_batching { pools: "us-west-2:gw-*" max_num_seqs: 8 max_batch_tokens: 2048 request_timeout_ms: 2000 prefix_kv_sync: false } ``` maya_oncall: who can push this config now? Need fast rollback if something breaks. arjun_runtime: I can cut the config and push to runtime-config. Will run canary on gw-9a, gw-9b, gw-9c (3 hosts). leo_support: ETA to customers? I'll prep a customer bulletin draft to CS once we confirm reduced error rate. arjun_runtime: pushing canary now — command: `rc push --env=prod --scope=us-west-2 --file=cb-hotfix.yaml --canary=3` jamie_sre: monitoring: watch evictions/sec, swap usage, 5xx rate per-tenant, and per-route latency P95. Also set alert to auto-rollback if 5xx rate increases vs baseline. incident-bot: config push started by arjun_runtime at 10:58:12 UTC — canary targets: gw-9a, gw-9b, gw-9c. arjun_runtime: canary applied to 3 hosts. Waiting 2 minutes for stabilization. maya_oncall: observed immediate drop in 502s on canary hosts, evictions down 70% on gw-9b. Nice. jamie_sre: scaling metrics look much healthier. Rolling to remaining hosts in pool with a 30s interval. Proceeding. ines_ops: rolling to rest of pool now (gw-9d..gw-9k) at low rate. leo_support: support note: errors dropping, customers confirming better response. Sending update to affected tenants: "We're rolling a hotfix to reduce batching pressure; you may see improved response times shortly." maya_oncall: customer impact quick note for incident report: 12 tenants affected, partial failures for ~45 minutes, error rate peaked at 7%, average extra latency 2.8x, no data loss. jamie_sre: post-rollout check — kv cache miss rate normalized, paging latency back to baseline, no elevated swap. We'll keep the config until we ship a gated PR that prevents global default drift. arjun_runtime: opened PR to add env-scoped defaulting and validation for continuous-batching config. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/8123 tanya_ml: we should add workload-level limits too (per-tenant max_seqs) to avoid noisy-neighbor packing. I'll coordinate with model-platform. devex_kate: small docs note: adding a checklist for runtime-config PRs that change defaults. I'll draft and link to the incident postmortem. maya_oncall: timeline summary for postmortem: - 10:45 UTC — traffic spike + config drift leads to higher max_num_seqs in prod - 10:50 UTC — KV cache eviction/paging spike observed, 502s begin - 10:53 UTC — PD alert escalated to oncall - 10:58 UTC — hotfix config pushed (canary 3 hosts) - 11:02 UTC — canary stable, rolling to pool; errors decline - 11:15 UTC — pool roll complete, metrics normalized leo_support: any immediate customer follow-ups needed? CS asks if we can offer credits for impacted jobs. maya_oncall: we'll include impact and mitigation in the incident report and run it by support leadership for credits. No auto-crediting yet. jamie_sre: action items: (1) revert global default in config repo, (2) add validation to runtime-config service, (3) add per-tenant packing limits, (4) publish runbook update for continuous-batching rollbacks. arjun_runtime: I'm owner for items 1 & 2, ETA EOD today for the config PR and guardrails. tanya_ml: I'll own per-tenant limits design, pairing with arjun for rollout plan. devex_kate: I'll update the ops runbook and create an internal KB: "Contbatch misconfig — hotfix & rollback steps." maya_oncall: final status — incident resolved, SLOs restored. I'll convert to an official postmortem and assign owners. Great job triaging and fast rollback. :tada: incident-bot: Incident closed by maya_oncall at 11:23:45 UTC — severity downgraded to sev-3 for postmortem.

top_candidates.title: incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache cardinality spike on inference-runtime-us-west-2 (affecting long-context requests). Paging oncall_jasper and eng_evan. Please acknowledge and triage. oncall_jasper: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and health dashboards now. sre_maria: I'm looking at the KV metrics — unique keys spiked by ~12x starting 1778501100, memory pressure on nodes hitting 92%. Continuous-batching queue depth also climbed. Possible correlation with yesterday's alpha longctx rollout (NTK/YaRN sliding window enabled). eng_evan: confirming: we pushed the sliding-window KV feature to alpha for ~50 customers at 03:00 UTC (NTK=4096, yarn-window=64). Metrics show a big increase in prefix cache entries for longctx requests. Looks like the sliding window is creating many small KV entries instead of reusing prefixes. prod_ryan: Customer impact? any 5xxs or timeouts reported to support? cs_ana: Support queue has 7 tickets flagged critical, a couple customers reported elevated latencies for batch chat endpoints. No full outages yet but increased errors on retries for some tenants. oncall_jasper: reading traces: tail of requests shows repeated cache misses -> regen -> regen -> cache insert thrash. Latency cliff at p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~1.1s. Need a mitigation plan now: reduce cardinality, throttle longctx path, and add KV eviction pressure relief. sre_maria: Proposed immediate mitigations (can do in order): 1) Disable sliding-window KV feature flag (alpha) -> stops new pathological entries. 2) Flush/Ring-fence KV cache for affected node pools to reclaim memory. 3) Apply runtime throttle: cap continuous batch size and reduce batch window from 20ms -> 5ms. 4) If needed, scale up Dedicated node pool as emergency capacity. eng_evan: I can flip the feature flag to off for alpha within 60s. Will prepare rollout to avoid global blip (canary across 1 AZ first). oncall_jasper: Do steps 1 and 3 first. Steps 2/4 if memory stays high. Assigning tasks: evan -> ff toggle, maria -> run cache flush+monitor, jasper -> change batching config and watch traces. eng_evan: toggling feature flag: `PATCH /flags/alpha/feature-sliding-window {"enabled": false}` infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for feature-sliding-window toggle -> canary in us-west-2a eng_evan: canary success, rolling to remaining alpha tenants. Confirmed patch applied at 1778501312. sre_maria: observed immediate reduction in new KV key churn after 1778501312. Memory pressure falling but still at ~78% across the pool. Continuous-batch queue depth dropped ~30%. oncall_jasper: applying continuous batching throttle now: set `CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256` and `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=5` on runtime config for longctx route. infra-bot: config-update: runtime-config longctx route updated. change recorded at 1778501420. sre_maria: after throttle: p95 latency improved to ~420ms, p50 ~190ms. Errors on retries dropped by ~60%. KV churn still present but much reduced. prod_ryan: good. any customer-facing actions? should we notify CS to message affected tenants? cs_ana: I'll prepare a short message: "We've applied mitigations to reduce elevated latency for long-context endpoints; engineering is monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for fixes." Sending to the 7 customers with tickets now. eng_evan: we should still do targeted cache eviction/compact for nodes that had the worst churn. maria, can you run a controlled flush on the top 3 nodes (rotate instead of global flush) to avoid cold start spikes? sre_maria: yes. I'll ring-fence the three highest-heat pods, evict local KV, and then bounce them one at a time: commands below. sre_maria: ``` # identify top pods kubectl get pods -l app=inference-runtime --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount | tail -n 3 # run eviction kubectl exec -it pod/rt-pod-123 -- /opt/runtime/bin/kv-evict --pattern="sliding:*" --force # restart pod kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=rt-pod-123 ``` infra-bot: eviction jobs queued on pods: rt-pod-123, rt-pod-119, rt-pod-102 sre_maria: evictions done; pods restarted sequentially. memory on those pods now ~30% reduced. No spike in 5xx during restarts. oncall_jasper: summary so far: feature flag off, batch throttle applied, targeted evictions + pod restarts. System stabilized but we should keep this incident open while monitoring for 60m and schedule follow-ups. eng_evan: follow-up action items: 1) fix sliding-window implementation to avoid high-cardinality keys (de-dupe prefixes, increase chunking granularity), 2) add guardrails in runtime to reject extreme NTK requests from alpha by default, 3) add cardinality alarm for KV namespace with auto-throttle. sre_maria: logging/alerts: raising a new alert rule: KV_unique_keys_rate > 3x baseline for 5m -> pager to sre. prod_ryan: customer impact note for postmortem: 7 CS tickets, latency increase for 50 alpha tenants, a handful of retries/partial failures. No broad outage. We'll classify as Sev2. cs_ana: messages sent to affected customers. waiting for replies. oncall_jasper: can we close the pager now or hold until 1778503234? I'll keep it open until last_message_ts per runbook (monitoring window is 33m). If stable at 1778503234 we'll close and draft postmortem. incident-bot: Reminder: incident window ends at 1778503234. Please update incident doc with timeline and follow-ups. sre_maria: adding timeline note: root cause linked to sliding-window kv behavior + NTK setting; mitigation steps executed and validated; follow-ups assigned to eng_evan and eng_platform for hardening. eng_evan: I'll open a PR with tests that simulate high-cardinality prefix workloads and require performance gates before alpha rollout. ETA EOD. oncall_jasper: ack. thanks team. I'll start the postmortem draft after the monitoring window closes. leaving thread for any late updates. cs_ana: FYI — one customer has replied saying latencies back to normal, thanked us. Closing customer updates. incident-bot: Incident thread will be archived after postmortem is attached. Good job coordinating. :tada:

top_candidates.title: title: Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF) — Launch & Operations Manual Overview This document describes the Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF), an opt-in program that supports cross-team skills development, rapid onboarding into adjacent domains, and internal mobility at Redwood. The RPF is a 6–12 week, project-oriented rotation designed for ICs and early managers who want hands-on experience in a different product area, platform team, or customer success track while keeping their core role and compensation intact. Purpose and goals - Accelerate skill acquisition for high-impact, cross-functional projects. - Reduce time-to-contribution when employees move to new teams or take on hybrid responsibilities. - Improve internal mobility rates and reduce hiring ramp costs. - Create repeatable handoff artifacts and templates that preserve institutional knowledge. Program variants - Short Fellowship (6 weeks): Focused learning sprint with one well-scoped deliverable. Best for tooling, docs, or experiment-driven work. - Standard Fellowship (9 weeks): Balanced discovery + delivery rhythm; includes a small end-to-end feature or migration task. - Deep Fellowship (12 weeks): For complex integrations, security/compliance projects, or multi-team migration planning. Eligibility and nomination - Who can apply: Regular ICs (L2–L5), staff-level engineers with manager consent, product managers, and member-of-staff customer success leads. - Manager approval: A written manager sign-off is required and must include a statement of support and a continuity plan for the fellow's home responsibilities. - Skill fit: Fellowship proposals must map to at least two measurable learning objectives and one deliverable for the host team. - Frequency: An individual may participate in the RPF up to twice in any 24-month period; exceptions require director-level approval. Key roles and responsibilities - Fellow (participant) - Own learning objectives, attend host team ceremonies, and deliver the agreed project artifact. - Maintain weekly updates to the home manager and host lead. - Home manager - Provide approval, maintain backfill plan (short-term coverage or task reprioritization), and maintain performance context. - Host lead - Assign a mentor, define the scope, and ensure access to systems and documentation. - Mentor (primary contact on the host team) - Provide day-to-day guidance, onboarding to codebase and tooling, and review deliverables. - People Ops (program owner) - Coordinate nominations, maintain fellowship schedule, run kickoff and wrap ceremonies, and keep program metrics. Selection process and timeline 1. Proposal submission (Week -3 to -2): Fellow or manager submits a 1-page proposal: goals, proposed host team, duration, and success criteria. 2. Triage (Week -2): People Ops validates eligibility and confirms host team capacity. 3. Approvals (Week -2 to -1): Home manager and host lead sign the rotation agreement. 4. Kickoff (Day 0): Program kickoff with People Ops, host mentor, fellow, and home manager. Agree on communication cadence, tooling access, and handoff milestones. 5. Midpoint check-in (Week 3–6): Formal review between the fellow, mentor, and home manager to adjust scope if needed. 6. Wrap & knowledge transfer (Final week): Document handoff, close tickets, and present outcomes at a cross-team demo. Rotation agreement template (1-page) - Title: [Fellow name] — [Host team] — [Duration] - Learning objectives: • Objective 1 • Objective 2 - Deliverable(s): • Artifact A (link) • Artifact B (link) - Duration and schedule: [start date] — [end date], expected weekly hours committed to host - Success criteria: 3 measurable acceptance checks - Approvals: Home manager | Host lead | People Ops Access and tooling checklist (example table) | Category | Items | Responsible | Target complete | |---------|-------|-------------|----------------| | Codebase | Repo access (read/write), CI runner tokens | Host lead | Day 2 | | Jira | Project write access, issue templates | Host lead | Day 2 | | Slack | Host team channel + #rpf-fellows | People Ops | Day 1 | | Cloud / Infra | Role-based access, test environment | Host lead + Security | Day 3 | | Analytics | Dashboard viewers, query access | Host lead | Day 4 | Onboarding & first-week cadence - Day 0: Kickoff meeting, rotation agreement sign-off, access checklist start. - Day 1–2: Codebase walkthrough, repo onboarding, run a local dev build, join host team standup and planning. - Day 3–5: Shadow mentor on core workflows, pick up first small task, weekly 1:1 scheduled with home manager and mentor. Performance management and compensation - The fellow remains on their home manager's org and payroll; there is no compensation change for standard rotations. - Performance feedback for the rotation is fed into the fellow's regular performance cycle by the home manager; the host lead provides a written rotation evaluation for the fellow's file. - Promotions and role changes resulting from the rotation are handled through standard promotion/transfer processes and require manager/director approval. Reporting, success metrics, and program KPIs People Ops will track and publish the following quarterly: - Fellowship count and completion rate (target completion >= 90%). - Average time to first meaningful contribution on host team (target <= 3 weeks for 6–9 week rotations). - Internal mobility conversion: percent of fellows who transfer roles within 12 months (target 18%+). - Fellow satisfaction (post-fellow NPS; target >= 8/10). - Document artifact quality: percent of handoffs with complete docs and runbooks (target >= 95%). Knowledge capture and handoff requirements - Every fellowship must close with a Confluence handoff page located under: /confluence/teams/[host-team]/rpf-handoffs/[fellow-name]-YYYYMMDD. - Required artifacts: - Architecture decision notes or design doc - Runbooks for anything operated in production - Test plan and known failure modes - A clear list of tickets left open and who will own them post-rotation Budgeting and perks - People Ops maintains a small rotation budget for cross-team learning. Typical reimbursable items include conference passes (pre-approved), short dedicated training, and workspace ergonomics for a remote fellow. - Fellows are eligible for a one-time learning stipend (up to $800) to cover books, courses, or small equipment purchases, pending manager sign-off. - Hosts can request a temporary headcount shadow (up to 2 weeks) for critical backfill; approvals routed through People Ops. Risk management and security - Sensitive projects (PII, audited) require a security review prior to approval. Host lead must list data accesses and sign off with Security. - If a rotation overlaps scheduled on-call windows, explicit contingency coverage must be documented before Day 0. - Hosts are responsible for ensuring fellows follow the host team's incident escalation and access policies. Wrap ceremony and knowledge sharing - All completed fellowships are celebrated in the RPF wrap ceremony (monthly hybrid town hall) where fellows present a 10-minute demo and learning recap. - Post-fellow writeups are published to a shared RPF Confluence space and linked to the home manager's performance notes. Measurement and continuous improvement - People Ops will run bi-annual retrospectives with host leads and a representative set of fellows to iterate on the program. - The RPF handbook will be updated annually or following significant process changes. FAQs - Q: Can fellows be on partial rotations (e.g., 50% time)? - A: Yes, with explicit manager and host lead approval; these are considered "embedded rotations" and require a more detailed continuity plan. - Q: Does the fellow keep their equity vesting schedule? - A: Yes, compensation and equity schedules are unchanged. - Q: Who owns the final deliverable? - A: The host team owns the deliverable post-handoff unless otherwise negotiated in the rotation agreement. Related links and templates - Rotation agreement template: /confluence/templates/rpf-agreement - Confluence handoff template: /confluence/templates/rpf-handoff - People Ops program calendar: /confluence/people-ops/rpf-schedule Stakeholders and escalation - Program owner: People Ops (Primary contact: people-ops@redwood.ai) - Escalations: Home manager -> Host lead -> Director of People Ops - Security review: Security (security@redwood.ai) for regulated projects Revision history - 2028-02-15: Version 1.0 — initial published manual (People Ops author) - 2028-03-01: Version 1.1 — clarified embedded rotation policy and added stipend details
