top_candidates.title: sam: Hey team — quick sync: we have a customer on Dedicated who hit capacity and got routed to Hosted, but the model variant on Hosted was a smaller quantized variant and the outputs were subtly different. Customer flagged it as a data-sensitivity concern. How should we handle routing when variant compatibility isn't exact? :thinking: elaine: Ugh. Was that routed by the current "tiered-fallback" policy? I thought Dedicated tenants could opt-out of spillover to Hosted. sam: They did not opt-out. Default is allow_spillover = true for mid-tier. They expected functional parity though. ravi: Two quick axes: (1) policy surface (console + API) vs org defaults, (2) telemetry/traceability so we can show customers what variant served them. We should fail closed if strict_isolation=true and otherwise attach routing_reason. alex: +1 on routing_reason. We also need a compatibility matrix check at routing time: if hosted variant model.arch != dedicated.model.arch or quant != quant we should either (a) refuse, (b) degrade gracefully with explicit header, or (c) fall back to a compatible hosted variant. Which is preferred? maria: For regulated customers, default should be refuse (reject) unless they explicitly allow variant-relaxed fallback. For mid-market, maybe allow but mark in console and send audit event. sam: Implementation idea: add a pre-routing hook that emits an event: {tenant, requested_variant, candidate_variant, compatibility_score, routing_decision}. Console shows per-request the last routing_decision and a link to the eval set used. Example event payload we could emit: { "tenant_id": "acct_ABC", "requested_model": "redwood/dedicated-xl-v2", "candidate_model": "redwood/hosted-xlq-quant", "compatibility_score": 0.72, "routing_decision": "spillover_with_variant_warning" } ravi: We should keep the schema minimal but searchable in logs. Suggest fields: routing_reason, variant_delta (enum: arch_mismatch, quant_diff, seq_len_limit), compatibility_score, override_flag. elaine: UX question: where does the customer configure this? Console toggle per-tenant + API field per-request? We need both. Per-request override should be rate-limited and audited. alex: Console affordance: add a toggle "Allow variant-relaxed spillover" (off by default for enterprise). Also surface last N routed requests with their routing_reason and compatibility_score. Add a big red badge when any routed request had variant_delta != none. maria: Also need a billing note: if the hosted variant has different perf/cost, we should surface potential cost delta on console and in invoice events. ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolled out routing_reason field to staging at 2130001100. Watch logs: /staging/routing/events sam: Nice. Edge-case: what if dedicated capacity is available but slow; should we prefer lower latency hosted variant over a busy dedicated? We currently route by priority: dedicated > hosted, but we could route by expected tail latency vs SLO. ravi: We can compute expected_latency = queue_time + p95_inference for variant. Add a policy expression: route_if(expected_latency(hosted) < expected_latency(dedicated) * 0.9 AND compatibility_score >= 0.9). That lets us choose hosted for latency-sensitive bursts. elaine: That policy sounds powerful but complex. Need to expose a safe default and a "policy editor" for advanced teams. Also need simulation UI: show hypothetical routing outcomes for last 24h. alex: Telemetry: add a tag on token-level logs: "served_variant" and "requested_variant", plus a trace_id linking request->fallback decision path. This makes debugging customer-reported regressions possible. maria: Ops-wise, we must ensure hosted variants serving PII-sensitive tenants are not used unless allowed. Add check: tenant_data_classification != pii OR allow_relaxed_spillover = true. sam: Action items: - [ ] add routing_reason, variant_delta, compatibility_score to routing events (ravi+alex) - [ ] console toggle and history UI (elaine+maria) - [ ] per-request API override + audit (alex) - [ ] default policy change for enterprise tenants to refuse (sam) - [ ] billing exposure for variant cost delta (maria) - [ ] add simulation in Console for policy changes (elaine) ravi: I'll draft the event schema tonight and post here. Also adding a small proposal for the compatibility_score heuristic: match on architecture, tokenizer, quantization, and output-stability evals. sam: Thanks. Let's keep default behavior conservative: reject for high-sensitivity customers, otherwise allow with warning and strong telemetry. :thumbsup: ops-bot: note: follow-up doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/routing/variant-fallback-proposal (draft)

top_candidates.title: ana: quick thought — proposal to relax embeddings endpoint so clients can send mixed-dim arrays if they opt in via header. router would split into uniform sub-batches and route per-model. avoids a lot of 413 churn for multi-model clients. sam: how do we bill/charge for splits? we'd need predictable quota semantics or we'll get support tickets. ana: plan: bill per original item using the target model's unit price. for splitter-generated child requests we emit telemetry linking child -> parent ID so usage and billing are reconciled server-side. clients still see single response. jordan: worry: splitting adds overhead and hurts batching efficiency. our load tests for runtime splitter showed ~3% 95p token latency increase on p3-like nodes. meera: console/telemetry needs: show split_rate, avg_splits_per_request, and per-split latency histogram. also surface percentage of requests that had partial failures. we should add a column in per-route table: "split enabled". ana: implementation notes: ``` Header: X-Embeddings-Allow-Split: true Payload: { "inputs": [[...],[...]], "model": "embed-large" } Router: if mixed dims -> create child reqs grouped by dims -> forward Response: 200 + { "results": [...], "split_info": { "children": 3, "partial_failures": [] } } ``` sam: partial failures — do we return 207 Multi-Status or always 200 with per-item status? returning 207 breaks a lot of SDKs. meera: prefer 200 with per-item status array. then console can show failure rate. SDKs parse it as normal. jordan: canary suggestion: feature flag default-off for hosted; enable for dedicated customers by config first. tag telemetry: split_feature=canary-<id>. rollout only after we have split-aware batching in runtime. infra-bot: load-test comment: "splitter + per-child routing" increased CPU on router by 8% and added 0.5ms to median request path in our 50k req/s test. (perf-run id: perf/2026-03-12/43) sam: need billing docs change: if child fails we still charge for successful children. if parent-level timeout occurs before children finish we prorate recorded tokens. I'll draft language. meera: UX: add a small indicator on route details: "split enabled (canary)" and a histogram for split_count; add alert if split_rate > 10% and 95p latency regresses > 2x compared to baseline. jordan: I'll prototype router split + telemetry events this week. can follow this cf-branch: feature/embed-splitter. I'll post PR with perf numbers. ana: action items: jordan prototype, meera console metrics + alert rules, sam billing blurb, i'll write RFC and include traffic model + SLO targets. :thumbsup: sam: :thumbsup: thanks. can we also log a sample of original payloads that trigger split for 24h for debugging? redaction required. ana: yes — sample at 0.1% with PII redaction. will include in RFC. meera: ok, i'm adding telemetry fields: ["parent_request_id","child_request_ids","split_count","split_reason","split_enabled_flag"], will send schema. jordan: noted. I'll tag all child requests with parent_request_id and split_version. ana: cool. I'll open the RFC tomorrow and cc infra/product. end.

top_candidates.title:
elaine_pm: Quick sync 011: EU enterprise wants an A/B experiment for the new routing policy but insists: no cross-border logs, and automatic user-facing fallback if latency > 300ms p95 for 3m. How do we design the rollout?

mike_research: key asks: 1) per-tenant/region A/B assignment, 2) telemetry bounded to EU KMS, 3) deterministic opt-in/opt-out for customers.

nora_eng: engineering constraints: we have per-tenant flags and region routing already. A/B split can be done via the routing layer but need deterministic hashing + sticky assignment. We should avoid global KV for assignments to keep EU data local.
luis_sre: ops concerns: automatic user-visible fallback for latency spikes is risky unless we have a cascading rollback plan. propose two-tier fallback: soft degrade (route to cheaper model variant) then hard fallback (route to legacy routing) if soft degrade doesn't recover in 5m.
elaine_pm: agree two-tier fallback is sensible. customers prefer immediate visible fallback vs silent regressions. we should include customer-facing banner in UI when fallback happens.
mike_research: for A/B metrics: primary KPI = latency p95 and error rate, secondary = model quality delta (via sample evaluation hooks). Need test harness to sample outputs and run gold prompts.
nora_eng: implementation sketch: 1) A/B assignment in-region using tenant_id % 100 < X. 2) telemetry aggregated by EU-only collectors -> KMS in EU. 3) gating service evaluates sliding windows of metrics and emits actions: NOOP / SOFT_DEGRADE / HARD_FALLBACK / ROLLBACK.
luis_sre: thresholds proposal: if p95 > 300ms for 3m -> SOFT_DEGRADE; if p95 stays > 350ms or error-rate > 2% for 5m -> HARD_FALLBACK. automated rollback if user-visible errors > 5% or user complaints flagged via support integration.
elaine_pm: regulatory check: legal insists the audit log for experiments be stored in EU for EU customers. prodops, can we automate that?
nora_eng: yes we can write experiment events to EU-only logging pipeline when tenant.region == "EU". small change in event producer, ETA 1 sprint.
prodops-bot: Reminder: create calendar block for "EU A/B bake (prod)" and include oncall; add runbook link. (automated)
mike_research: can we do a shadow run first? send 100% traffic in shadow to new routing and collect latency/quality without impacting users. then flip % of traffic in small increments: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> full. each step gated by metric windows.
luis_sre: agree on shadowing first. Also request: add a canary host pool that isolates model variant under test to avoid cache contamination.
elaine_pm: decision checklist for this thread: 1) require EU-local telemetry+audit for EU tenants, 2) shadow test then phased %-ramp with deterministic in-region assignment, 3) two-tier fallback (soft degrade to cheaper variant, then hard fallback to legacy), 4) automated gating + rollback thresholds as proposed. any objections?
nora_eng: no objections. will draft spec: routing-hash details, event tagging, canary pool config.
mike_research: no objections. I'll prepare evaluation prompt set and acceptance criteria for quality delta.
luis_sre: no objections. I'll write the rollback runbook and thresholds into SRE playbooks.
elaine_pm: next steps: nora to open spec PR and link canary config; mike to upload eval suite; luis to add runbook and pager triggers. weekly check-in Thurs 10:30.
prodops-bot: Action items created: #4821 spec PR, #4822 eval suite, #4823 rollback runbook. (automated)
elaine_pm: thanks team. I'll notify EU customer and align timelines.

top_candidates.title: Marta: Heads up — thinking about adding small routing/quota + telemetry annotations to saved views. Idea: saved views carry a lightweight "hints" section with sampling, preferred route, and quota estimate. Wanted reactions before I spin up an API PR. Jordan: ++ need this for rollout gating. If a saved view can say 'sample_rate: 5%' we can auto-apply higher-fidelity telemetry during experiments without manual toggles. Matt: UX thought — compact badge on saved view card: 'Q:5% | S:10k' or 'route: r196'. Click -> preview implications modal. Keep main list uncluttered. Lee: API note — we'd need to extend the savedquery schema. Two approaches: embed metadata in existing object or have a separate viewHints resource. I lean separate to avoid breaking clients. Simone: Telemetry caveat — sample rate is not monolithic. Traces vs token-level vs eval sampling all differ. We need clear keying. Marta: Good point. Proposal (simple): keys: routing_hint (route_id), quota_est (tokens_per_min), telemetry_sample:{type:rate}. Example: ```{ "routing_hint":"route-196", "quota_est":"1200tpm", "telemetry_sample":{ "trace":"1%", "eval":"10%" } }``` Lee: Implementation nit — our persisted schema prefers flat columns. Nested telemetry_sample will mean special parsing. I suggest flattened keys like telemetry_trace_sample and telemetry_eval_sample. top_candidates.title: alex: FYI — we need a quick cross-team sync on the new error taxonomy metrics before the canary rollout next week. main asks: consistent names, dashboard panels, and which signals the console will use for degraded-mode UX. maria: Agree. Biggest open questions: 1) What counts as a fallback vs degraded mode? 2) Do we emit per-model or per-route counts? 3) How do quotas feed into routing decisions (reject vs queue)? sam: For counting: suggest these metrics - runtime.error.timeout_total - runtime.error.5xx_total - runtime.oom_total - runtime.fallback.count - routing.quota.rejected_total - routing.quota.queued_current We should include labels: model, route, region, tier ingrid: +1. Also include a boolean label 'degraded=true' when we return a graceful fallback so dashboards can differentiate hard failures vs graceful degraded responses. ryan: Console/UX note: we want a single 'Reliability' card that shows 3 small panels: latency/timeouts, 5xx rate, fallback rate. Fallback rate should be normalized per successful responses AND per attempted requests — otherwise it confuses users. devex: For SDKs we can surface a simple API: client.metrics.increment("fallback", {model, route, reason:"cache_miss"}) and have server translate to runtime.fallback.count; but we need a spec for accepted labels. sam: Proposal for PromQL snippets to standardize panels: # fallback rate per minute per route sum(rate(runtime_fallback_count{route!="",region="$region"}[1m])) by (route) / sum(rate(requests_total{route!="",region="$region"}[1m])) by (route) # 5xx rate sum(rate(runtime_error_5xx_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(requests_total[route!=""][5m])) by (route) maria: Good. Need to decide aggregation for quotas. I propose: - routing.quota.rejected_total{route,quota_name} - routing.quota.queued_current{route} And an alert if rejected_total rate spikes > 0.5% of requests for 15m. ingrid: On the runtime side, OOMs are noisy. We should emit both container-ish OOMs and model-serve OOMs: runtime.oom_total{oom_type="container"|"model"}. That will help SRE triage. alex: Cross-team action items: - eng-runtime: emit the metrics listed with labels (model, route, region, tier, degraded, reason) - eng-platform: provide standardized PromQL and dashboard templates - console: wire the 3-panel reliability card and the alerting thresholds - devex: publish SDK metric helpers + label schema Can people ack and add owners? ryan: Console owner for wiring: ryan — will add panels and create a JSON dashboard template that can be parameterized by org and region. sam: runtime owner: sam — will start a PR to export the metrics with the agreed labels. I'll add instrumented places for fallback increments and OOM tagging. ingrid: SRE/infra owner: ingrid — will verify OOM metrics and add a node-level fallback to ignore infra-level OOMs in the model-level graphs. devex: i'll own the SDK helpers and docs (devex). will open a spec doc with expected labels. maria: i'll own alerting thresholds and rollout plan for alerts (prod-safe gradual increase). will coordinate with ryan for console alert UI. alex: timeline: get metric exports by EOD Wed, dashboard/json templates by Fri, alert PRs early next week. if blockers surface, ping #eng-oncall and drop a short thread here. deploy-bot: milestone created: "reliability-metrics-rollout" assigned to alex, sam, ryan, ingrid, devex, maria ryan: quick UX question — do we want a per-route toggle in the console to hide low-traffic routes? otherwise the panel noise is bad. I propose default: show top 10 routes by request volume, with an expandable list. maria: yes please. also add breadcrumbs to go from a route panel to the model-specific timeline and the request traces link. alex: perfect. last ask: include an example payload spec in the dashboard doc for how the console will fetch aggregated metrics (time window, group_by labels, top_k param). devex/sam can pair on that. sam: noted. i'll include example API contract in the PR: /api/internal/metrics/aggregate?from=...&to=...&group_by=route,model&top_k=10 devex: ack, pairing session thursday morning? ryan: ack, thursday 10am works. i'll draft dashboard skeleton before then. ingrid: i'll run a short loadtest to ensure the new counters don't regress runtime perf; will report any cardinality issues. alex: thanks everyone — let's follow up in the PRs. cc @oncall if anything spikes during rollout.

Paging on-call. maria_g: acked, jumping in. seeing ~25% errors, latency spike to 2.1s p95. devon_s: on it — I'm pulling routing metrics and smart-routing decision logs. sre_lead: quick checklist: (1) scope customers impacted (2) confirm whether fallbacks triggered (3) validate DNS/edge. maria_g: customer-impact quick note: traffic to hosted-api eu region. Some requests routed to a model variant tagged `gptt-2-small` which we decommissioned last week — that could explain validation errors. eng_prod: wait, why would smart-routing pick `gptt-2-small`? policy should prefer matching model-tag then fallback to nearest region. Did a policy change go out? devon_s: pulling policy history... found a config push 45m ago that updated fallback chain for eu -> global -> us-east. looks normal. but routing logs show requests for eu being resolved to endpoint eu-edge-old.rwd.ai (decom) maria_g: DNS check from a few edge nodes: `dig +short eu.service.rwd.ai` -> returns CNAME to `eu-edge-old.rwd.ai` for some resolvers, `eu-edge-new.rwd.ai` for others. inconsistent. TTLs on the old records were 1h. ops_bot: system note: CDN invalidation completed 2h ago for eu-edge-new, but DNS change didn't propagate fully — looks like resolver caches holding old CNAME. sre_lead: hmm that explains routing loop: old edge is returning a healthy route but it's connected to retired compute pools referencing the old model variant. Smart-routing sees endpoint up -> routes -> inference fails -> fallback triggers -> routes again -> oscillation. devon_s: logs snippet: ``` [router] decision: prefer eu-edge-old.rwd.ai -> send to host 10.12.3.45 [host] model-check: variant gptt-2-small not available -> error 422 [router] fallback: route -> global-edge-1 -> global-edge-1 resolves back to eu-edge-old via DNS ``` maria_g: mitigation plan step 1: prevent routing loops by temporarily locking fallback policy to prefer-primary-region and disable circular fallback for eu for next 30m. Can someone apply? eng_prod: I'm applying the policy lock now via console and CLI. `redwoodctl routing set-policy eu --fallback-policy prefer-primary --disable-circular-true --note "incident 1782102468"` eng_prod: done. policy change rolled out to routers (prop 1). sre_lead: step 2: reduce DNS TTLs to 30s and force purge old CNAMEs from known public resolvers where possible. ops, can you coordinate with CDN/DNS provider? ops_bot: contacting provider support (ticket #CDN-58421). Meanwhile forcing purge on CloudEdge: `cloudedge purge eu-edge-old.rwd.ai` -> response: queued. devon_s: writing a query to count affected requests by origin resolver: `select count(*) from router_logs where region='eu' and upstream_host='eu-edge-old.rwd.ai' and status>=500 since -60m` -> ~43k requests. Error rate ~22% overall for region. maria_g: customer impact estimate: ~3.5% of total hosted API customers saw increased error rates for ~46 minutes. Noting a few high-volume customers reported 5xx spikes. sre_lead: good. step 3 rollback: point any smart-routing entries referencing `eu-edge-old` to `eu-edge-new` immediately. eng_prod, can you push a route override? eng_prod: pushing route override: `redwoodctl routing override set --host eu-edge-old.rwd.ai --target eu-edge-new.rwd.ai --ttl 60` -> rolled to all routing proxies. maria_g: verifying with `curl -v https://eu.service.rwd.ai/health` from multiple nodes — now resolves to eu-edge-new for 9/10 nodes, last one still showing old -> waiting for purge. devon_s: also noticed in traces that fallback policy was mis-evaluating model-variant compatibility because of a mapping file `/etc/redwood/model_variant_map.json` on the old pool that included `gptt-2-small`. That file should have been removed during decommission. sre_lead: assign owner to clean decommission artifacts: tim_k take point with infra to ensure no stray mapping files remain on retired pools. tim_k: on it — kicking a job to sweep retired pools. `infra-cleanup --tag retired --check model_variant_map.json` -> queued. ops_bot: CDN purge completed for most POPs. provider reports positive propagation but some ISP caches still stubborn. maria_g: continuing monitoring. error rate trending down — now 7% and falling. p95 latency back to 450ms. devon_s: while we recover, recommend we keep the fallback lock for +30m and leave override in place for +60m. Also drop DNS TTL change to 15s if still flapping. sre_lead: agreed. extended locks applied. also opening an RCA ticket and a customer-impact tracker. please add any customers that submitted support tickets. eng_prod: adding quick mitigation note to status page: "Partial degradation for EU-hosted inference endpoints; mitigation in progress. No data loss; temporary routing policy enforced." :warning: maria_g: handoff to next on-call in 30 minutes. summary for oncall-next: root cause is stale DNS/CNAME pointing some resolvers to decommissioned edge which had leftover model variant mapping producing validation errors, creating fallback oscillation. top_candidates.title: maya: Heads up — after we pushed the 535.86 driver + CUDA 12.2 roll last night, we've got a regression: NVLink topology isn't being detected on mixed A100 nodes. NCCL falls back to SHM -> SOCKET for most peer transfers, huge perf hit. leo: which cluster/region? maya: prod-gpu-eu, also seeing on staging-us-west. Only on racks that have a mix of kernel versions (5.15.x + 6.1.x) and some older A100-SXM nodes. taylor: any logs or nccl topo dump? short snips are fine. maya: paste: ``` $ nvidia-smi topo --matrix GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 CPU GPU0 X NV PHB SYS GPU1 NV X PHB SYS GPU2 PHB PHB X SYS ``` but nccl shows: ``` NCCL INFO Topo: NVLINK not usable between 0 and 1 (p2p query failed) NCCL WARN All-to-all using SOCKET fallback for peer 0-1 NCCL INFO SHM disabled (IPC failure) ``` indra: SHM disabled often due to IPC namespace or missing /dev/shm mount in container. Are these in k8s pods with ipcMode? any change in runtime flags? maya: pods are default, we didn't change --ipc. Container runtime didn't update, only driver and kernel modules. dmesg on one node: ``` [ 428.123456] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: P2P peer lookup failed, peer 0000:3a:00.0 [ 428.123460] nvidia-mig: failed to query P2P capability ``` jun: Could be the kernel driver ABI mismatch — mixing dkms-built modules with packaged driver? Which package mechanism did we use for 535? rpm or runfile? maya: runfile installer (we used for faster rollout). Some older nodes still had kernel module from 525 and we forced install but didn't rebuild DKMS properly. leo: that explains P2P failures. If module symbols mismatch, NVLink P2P ioctl can fail and NCCL disables p2p. Workaround: put affected nodes into maintenance and roll back to 525, or rebuild kernel module via dkms and reboot. taylor: timeline wise, can we isolate by node label and cordon? Also we should avoid full rollback if we can hotfix: rebuild modules and restart kubelet + container runtime to rebind devices. maya: doing a canary: cordoned 2 nodes in prod-gpu-eu and initiated dkms rebuild + reboot. I'll report perf after. ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0783 - "NVLink/NCCL P2P regressions after 535 driver rollout". Pager on-call: leo, taylor. indra: another mitigation: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to force consistent path (explicit SOCKET) while we fix drivers — avoids random mixed behavior, but costs throughput. Also NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1 if IPC is flaky. jun: note: forcing SOCKET may hurt multi-node perf but keeps correctness; useful temporary flag for training jobs that can't tolerate nondeterministic fallbacks. maya: perf numbers after canary rebuild: peer bandwidth for single-GPU pairs went from 3.2 GB/s (socket fallbacks) back to 72 GB/s when NVLink restored. Good sign. taylor: good. Next steps: - create an automated check during driver rollout: run `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` + `nccl-tests` smoke to validate NVLink/SHM - add DKMS verification in rollout playbook - add node label to identify kernel-driver mismatches maya: I'll open a PR to update the rollout runbook + add a k8s admission job that checks /dev/shm and ipc namespace for GPU pods. leo: also add a step: if module version mismatch detected, mark node drainable and block burst autoscaler from placing new GPU pods. maya: noted. will follow up with timeline and postmortem notes. srebot: Deploy log: driver-rollout-2025-03-22 completed on 2025-03-22T02:13:00Z. 17 nodes patched, 4 nodes reported dkms mismatch. maya: thanks — tagging this thread for postmortem. Any objections to rolling back the remaining 3 mismatched nodes to 525-runfile and re-testing before reapplying 535 via dkms package? taylor: +1. safer and we can automate dkms-based rollout afterwards. leo: please include cost impact estimate in postmortem (retries + slower jobs). I expect ~12% longer training time for affected jobs in EU yesterday. maya: will include. closing the loop when PR/PM posted.

top_candidates.title:
incident-bot: ALERT: autoscaler-oscillation detected in prod (us-east-1). metric: gpu_pool_utilization. spikes -> rapid scale ups/downs causing request failures. paging ryan-oncall and team. incident id: INC-20260315-8423 :rotating_light:
ryan-oncall: got it. i'm oncall. looking at autoscaler metrics now. can someone post recent spike graphs?
erin-sre: pulling logs for the last 30m. seeing repeated scale events: scale_up -> scale_down loop. kube events show NodeJoin/NodeTerminate churn.
mike-rtc: seeing a correlated burst of short-lived batch jobs from a customer integration (internal-job-runner). sending link to logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/trace/abcd1234
kate-csm: FYI, CSM told me a few enterprise customers reported 502/503s around 09:42-09:58. one raised a support ticket (SUP-5492).
dmitri-eng: could be autoscaler cooldown too short + pod readiness flapping. what's current autoscaler config?
erin-sre: current config snippet: ```yaml
minReplicas: 2
maxReplicas: 50
scaleUpPolicy: immediate
scaleDownCooldown: 30s
scaleUpCooldown: 10s
```
that scaleDownCooldown is probably too aggressive for GPU nodes.
ryan-oncall: immediate mitigation attempt: disabling aggressive scaleDown for the pool and forcing stable size to 12 while we investigate. running: `redwood-cli pool set --name gpu-us-east-1 --target 12`
ops-bot: ACTION: pool gpu-us-east-1 target set to 12 by ryan-oncall. previous target 6.
sarah-qa: after scaling target to 12, error rate dropped to baseline ~1.2% within 3 minutes. looks like mitigation worked. :thumbsup:
kate-csm: passing update to affected customers, telling them we mitigated and investigating root cause.
jasmin-ops: planning post-incident review. prefer a short postmortem meeting today. who can join? propose 16:00 UTC.
dmitri-eng: I can join. want to review autoscaler tuning, job throttling, and add hard limits on short batch bursts.
erin-sre: will prepare timeline + extracted logs.
ryan-oncall: assign follow-ups here. immediate action items in-thread: 1) revert scaleDownCooldown to safer value and add min cooldown 5m for GPU pools (owner: erin-sre) 2) add request throttling to internal-job-runner to smooth bursts (owner: dmitri-eng) 3) create alert that detects >3 scale events in 10m for same pool (owner: mike-rtc) 4) customer comms recap (owner: kate-csm) 5) add canary for autoscaler config changes (owner: jasmin-ops)
erin-sre: creating ticket INFRA-2741 with details and immediate config change notes. linking runbook: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/autoscaler-runbook
mike-rtc: I will add the "oscillation" alert rule and a dashboard panel showing scale events per minute.
ops-bot: TASK CREATED: INFRA-2741 (autoscaler cooldown and remediation) assigned to erin-sre.
jasmin-ops: scheduled postmortem meeting 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC. invite sent to participants and stakeholders. meeting link: https://meet.internal/redwood/pm-INC-20260315-8423
dmitri-eng: quick note — internal-job-runner had a recent deployment that changed retry policy; rolling back might reduce the burst. I'll coordinate with platform team.
kate-csm: customer updates sent. two customers requested SLA credit evaluation; capturing in SUP-5492.
erin-sre: after mitigation, adding a short-term guard in autoscaler logic: disallow scaleDown if last scaleUp < 300s. pushing patch to staging and will roll to prod after smoke. snippet: ```go
if now.Sub(lastScaleUp) < 5*time.Minute {
 skipScaleDown()
}
```
ryan-oncall: nice. once patch is live, let's monitor for 24h. set a follow-up check in status board.
sarah-qa: will run synthetic traffic tests to ensure we don't regress (target windows: 10m bursts and steady).
jasmin-ops: postmortem owners: infra -> erin-sre (write prose + timeline), eng -> dmitri-eng (root cause analysis + mitigation), devex -> mike-rtc (alerts + dashboards), support -> kate-csm (customer comms). deadline for draft: 2026-03-18 EOD.
erin-sre: draft created at https://confluence.redwood/postmortems/INC-20260315-8423-draft. linking logs and timeline.
dmitri-eng: created remediation epic: EPIC-1210 (autoscaler hardening). will break into tasks and add estimated ETA.
ops-bot: REMINDER: postmortem draft due 2026-03-18.
ryan-oncall: final note — we should add autoscaler simulation tests in CI to catch oscillation patterns before prod. filing infra task.
jasmine-ops: (typo) jasmin-ops: moving thread to follow-up and closing active paging; will reopen if new problems. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-20260315-8423 status: mitigated — impact contained. severity: Sev2. closing page.
jasmin-ops: postmortem meeting notes will be appended to the confluence draft and action items tracked in EPIC-1210. thanks everyone for quick response.
ryan-oncall: handing off to erin-sre for follow-ups. I'm out of rotation.
erin-sre: ack. taking ownership of follow-ups. will post updates in INFRA-2741 as tasks progress.

top_candidates.title: oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert: incident PAGER-8243 triggered for cluster inference-prod. Symptoms: sudden spike in NCCL communicator errors and multi-GPU hangs, repeated container restarts on nodes gpu-12,gpu-13,gpu-17. Error rate > 20% for /v1/generate on model-xlarge-8way. Paging sre oncall now. sre_jamie: Ack. I'm on it. Can folks paste the latest pod logs for the failing rank? I want the first glimpse of the NCCL stack. ml_infra_lee: Pasting trimmed log from pod inference-runtime-xyz (rank 2): ``` [2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL WARN Unhandled cuda error, aborting [2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL ERROR ncclCommAbort called, communicator invalid [2026-03-15 02:45:21] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error' runtime_error: cudaLaunchKernel failed: out of resources at /workspace/runtime/collective/comm.c:412 at /usr/local/bin/inference-runtime ``` We're also seeing container restarts (`CrashLoopBackOff`) and occasional OOMs on the GPU when sequence length spikes. eng_omar: Likely bad interaction between kernel scheduling and tensor parallel communicator. Could be a race on communicator teardown when a pod gets preempted. Quick mitigation: reduce tensor-parallel degree for active model-route and shift traffic to a smaller single-gpu variant. I'll prepare route change if SRE gives go. sre_jamie: Immediate mitigation plan (proposed): 1) Temporarily mark the 3 problematic nodes unschedulable (cordon) to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 gpu-13 gpu-17`. 2) Drain the failing pods and restart the runtime on healthy nodes: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl delete pod -l app=inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-12` for each. 3) Apply fallback routing: shift 40% of traffic for model-xlarge-8way to model-xlarge-1gpu (lower throughput, safe single-gpu path). 4) If restarts persist, scale model instances down to TP_SIZE=1/PP_SIZE=1 for the route and restart the deployment. ml_infra_lee: Executed step 1 & 2 on gpu-12 and gpu-13. Logs show one node had `nvidia-driver` OOM trace and GPU driver process got killed. I cordoned gpu-17 but didn't drain yet (still serving). Sample command I ran: ``` kubectl cordon gpu-12 kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-xyz-2 ``` cs_tara: Any idea which customers hit 5xxs? AcmeFinance just flagged errors in prod. Need ETA to share with them. ml_infra_lee: From metrics: AcmeFinance and BetaRetail were the top two that hit elevated 5xx counts. Total user-facing error rate peaked ~18% on the route. After cordon+drain the error rate dropped to ~6% but still above baseline. eng_omar: I'm ready to change routing. If SRE confirms the partial reroute, I'll do a canary 20% -> 80% to test stability. sre_jamie: Do it. eng_omar make it 25/75 for 10 minutes, watch latency and error stream. deploy-bot: Routing update started by eng_omar: model-xlarge-8way -> 25% traffic to model-xlarge-1gpu. Rollout id: r-20260315-1759 ml_infra_lee: After routing shift we saw error rate go to ~2-3% but latency increased on the single-gpu path as expected. No more NCCL communicator aborts on nodes still serving. Meanwhile, pod restarts have stopped on gpu-12 and gpu-13. ops_maya: I suggest we also enable NCCL debugging envs on a staging replica to capture more info: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL`. Also consider setting `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` briefly to rule out p2p prob. sre_jamie: Good call. But don't flood prod logs. Run debug on a single canary pod in a non-customer shard. ml_infra_lee: Created a debug deployment `inference-debug-canary` with NCCL_DEBUG enabled and TP/PP set to same as prod. Collecting traces now. sre_jamie: Next steps for live mitigation: keep nodes cordoned, maintain 25/75 routing split, finish draining gpu-17 if safe, and run a controlled rollout with TP_SIZE=1 for model-xlarge across the cluster if we see reoccurrence. Also open a ticket for post-incident capacity adjustments. cs_tara: Sending a short customer update: "We're investigating elevated errors on model-xlarge; traffic has been partially rerouted to a stable variant and we're working on node restarts. ETA 1h for remediation" — ok to send? sre_jamie: OK to send. Add note that some customers may see higher latency. pagerduty: On-call handoff: sre_jamie -> ops_maya at 03:15 UTC. Handoff acknowledged. PagerDuty note: continue mitigation, collect debug logs, and escalate to HW vendor if driver kills persist. ops_maya: Took over. Running NVIDIA diagnostics on gpu-17 now (`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CEC,PERSISTENCE`). One node shows ECC corrected errors increasing. ml_infra_lee: ECC counts rising on gpu-17, and dmesg shows multiple `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` entries. I queued a maintenance for that host with infra: HOST-REPLACE-178. eng_omar: Given suspected hardware instability, we should automate fallback routing for high-latency/5xx spikes in future: if error-rate > 5% for 2m, automatically shift 50% traffic to single-gpu variant. Filing an RFC after mitigation. sre_jamie: Agreed. For now: drained gpu-17 and replaced 2 pods onto healthy nodes. Error rate back to baseline ~0.8%. We'll keep the cluster at reduced TP config overnight and schedule full postmortem. deploy-bot: Rollout complete: r-20260315-1759 -> routing now 10% single-gpu, 90% original (rollback in case of symptoms). All health checks green. ops_maya: Marking incident as mitigated. Creating a follow-up task: replace gpu-17 host, validate ECC and driver stability, and run a soak test for 6 hours with TP_SIZE=2. sre_jamie: Closing incident PAGER-8243 as mitigated. Action items: (1) Postmortem + timeline (owner: ml_infra_lee), (2) Auto-fallback RFC (owner: eng_omar), (3) Hardware replacement and soak (owner: ops_maya). I'm adding these to the incident ticket. cs_tara: Thanks team — will update AcmeFinance and BetaRetail that we've mitigated and will follow up with timeline and RCA. oncall-bot: Incident PAGER-8243 status -> mitigated. Incident postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC.

Attached verification checklist and screenshots. Alex Gomez: Deployed fixes contained in PR #2892 and #2901. Closing remediation subtasks, leaving dependency upgrades to a follow-up sprint. Priya Desai: Vendor risk confirmed binder accepted. Thanks everyone — will file closure note in vendor portal. Sam Patel: Closing loop here. Final artifacts attached to JIRA and vendor binder.

Could be slow downstream responses. mike: Runs: `curl -sS https://edge.east.health/metrics | jq '.connections'` shows many TIME_WAITs. Suspect connection churn to cache/backends. leila: Can we do a graceful failover to us-central while we investigate east? We should validate first with a synthetic canary. anne: Yes. Plan: create quick synthetic job in us-central to validate a few endpoints, then shift 30% traffic for 5m, watch p95 & 5xx, then increase. infra-bot: Command: `traffic-shift start --from=us-east1 --to=us-central1 --pct=30 --duration=5m --validate=synthetic-canary` ops-bot: Synthetic canary job `smoke-canary-us-central` created and executed: 10/10 requests OK, avg latency 210ms. raj: Canary good. Initiating shift. mike: Noting KV-cache miss rate in us-east1 increased by ~3x. Adding cache replica to east and throttling new connections from bursty clients. leila: Live mitigation: cache scaled +2, outbound connections for pool east-7 restarted to clear stuck connections. anne: After shift p95 in east dropped from 1.3s -> 780ms, 5xx dropped by 60%. Good. Holding shift at 70% to central to confirm stability. raj: Quick customer-impact note: a handful of sessions dropped between 20:05-20:12 UTC. Support ticketing group notified. leila: For follow-up: alert tuning needed - current latency alert fires on 1m window which causes churn. Propose: change latency -> 5m rolling p95 and require sustained deviation. Also add region-specific thresholds. mike: Suggest adding a Prometheus recording rule for regional p95 to speed queries and avoid flapping: ``` - record: regional:request_p95:5m expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region)) ``` leila: Also add an alert: `RegionalHighP95` with for: 10m, labels: severity=page if region QPS > baseline*0.2 else severity=warn. That reduces noise for low-traffic regions. raj: We should dedupe pages coming from multiple monitors for the same root cause (e.g., cache pressure). Proposing a new alertmanager grouping rule: group_by: ['cluster', 'region', 'alertname', 'cause_signature_hash'] anne: Add suppression during automated rollouts and traffic shifts to prevent paging for expected transient latencies. Mike take the recording rules & alerts. Raj take the dashboard. mike: I'll prototype the alert changes in staging and run a sensitivity sweep for false positives. Will post results. ops-bot: Incident timeline saved to incident-doc: https://redwood-internal/incidents/1802238890 (private) anne: Oncall handoff: I'll hand primary to raj in 90 minutes. Leaving detailed mitigations in the doc. raj: Taking handoff. Leaving a short checklist: monitor `regional:request_p95:5m`, `kv_cache_miss_total`, `tcp_time_wait_count`, and `edge_5xx_rate`. If any trend > 2x baseline, re-escalate. incident-bot: Incident resolved: auto-close after mitigation verified. time_to_ack: 2m, time_to_recover: 14m. Tags: regional-failover, alert-tuning, synthetic-canary leila: Quick retro note: need better pre-emptive canary coverage for all critical API paths. Incident ID INC-4299 Maria (oncall): ack. seeing p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 1.3s, streaming stall percentage ~4.2%. multiple customers reporting streaming interruptions (NimbusData, PaperclipAI). grabbing logs. Akshay: initial glance at routing weight tables shows a suspicious concentration. rolling-affinity v2 was promoted yesterday. I see many micro-weights assigned which might be colliding in the selector. Jess: router logs show repeated stream resets to the same shard id. sample lines: ``` [router] 2026-03-15T05:02:11Z POST /v1/stream id=cid-99 upstream=shard-42 status=200 stream-reset=1 latency_ms=1389 [model-proxy] 2026-03-15T05:02:11Z shard-42 queue=410 active=420 ``` This looks like queue buildup on shard-42. Carter (night-oncall): I'm in. which regions most impacted? Akshay: us-west-2 and eu-central show disproportionate hit-rate to shard-42 and shard-7. weight snapshot (excerpt): ``` shard-42: 0.00009 shard-7: 0.00010 shard-3: 0.99981 ``` Selector normalization uses a float->int floor which seems to bias mapping for certain prefixes; when many tiny weights exist, hashing modulo maps them to same low-id bucket. I can reproduce locally. Maria (oncall): mitigation options: (A) immediate rollback of rolling-affinity v2 to v1 (global), (B) apply emergency weight floor config (treat weights < 0.001 as 0) and re-normalize, (C) route-streams to bypass pool (force round-robin) for affected routes. Which gives fastest relief? Jess: canary rollback might take longer. emergency config floor is quickest. Ops-Runner can push config fast. Ops-Runner: I can push a config patch in ~4 mins. ready on go. Akshay: I'll assemble the config patch now — minimal change: treat tiny weights as zero and re-normalize across remaining shards. SRE-bot: config-push started (cfg-98890) by Akshay. expect propagation ~40-50s per zone. Maria (oncall): pushing Ops-Runner to scale streaming pool preemptively +2 replicas while patch propagates. Ops-Runner: scaling streaming-pool from 10 -> 12. Jess: canary nodes show p99 drop from ~1.3s -> 700ms. queue lengths on shard-42 drop from 410 -> 90. Good sign. SRE-bot: config-push rolled to 60% routers. Maria (oncall): global p95 now 210ms, p99 ~710ms, streaming stalls ~1.1%. improvement but still above SLO. Carter, take ownership for steady-state monitoring. I'll handoff. Carter (night-oncall): taking it. summary: emergency weight-floor applied; observe p99 and streaming stalls for 30m. run `redis-cli -h routing-store HGETALL weights:affinity:v2` and identify values < 0.001. run `scripts/hotmap.sh --window=10m` to produce hotkey map. Carter (night-oncall): hotmap shows shard-42 receiving ~58% of certain prefix hashes. Akshay: root cause hypothesis: selector normalization rounding bug causes many tiny weights to be represented similarly in the integer hashing domain, leading to mapping collisions and hot partitions. Repro steps and unit test added. Jess: action: open rollback PR if config patch doesn't finish improving within 15m. Also capture log buffer for 10m window for postmortem. Olivia (pm): customer impact: NimbusData claims ~12% sessions affected; we should notify customers on affected list and offer mitigation timeline. prepping comms. Maria (oncall): assign tasks: @Akshay to open PR with selector fix + tests, @Jess to run stress tests against fixed selector in staging, @Carter to draft incident notification and post to #incidents-notify, @Ops-Runner to keep scaling plan ready. Akshay: created PR https://git.company/repo/pulls/1430 with unit tests and changelog. requesting expedited review. will also add configuration assertion to reject configs with >30% total weight in micro-weight shards. SRE-bot: EVENT: mitigation_applied by Akshay at 2765439999. Carter (night-oncall): current metrics: 30m rolling p99 ~ 640ms, p95 205ms, streaming stalls 0.9%. Still above p99 SLO of 500ms. will monitor for 1h then re-evaluate rollback. Maria (oncall): leaving pager. Carter you're primary. escalate to oncall lead if p99 > 800ms for 15m. Carter (night-oncall): ack. posting interim incident note to #incidents-notify in 8m. Jess: note for postmortem: include timeline of config propagation across regions (we saw ~50s lag per zone) which impacted how fast canary improvement translated to global SLOs. Olivia (pm): scheduling follow-up with Support & Solutions at 09:00 UTC tomorrow to coordinate customer outreach. Akshay: additional temporary measure: add selector defensive code to treat weights <0.0005 as 0 and add telemetry to flag when >5% of config entries are micro-weights. will include in PR. Ops-Runner: scaled streaming pool +2 completed. SRE-bot: Pager cleared by Maria. Carter (night-oncall): marking incident mitigated for now. will keep monitoring and prepare postmortem draft. adding backlog items: full rollback exercise, more robust selector tests, telemetry for micro-weight configs. Maria (oncall): great work team. keep an eye on customer tickets and confirm any required credits or remediation.

Combined with continuous batching config (max_batch_tokens=2048) we might be retaining much bigger KV for long-lived sessions. lily: customers affected: heavy-chat customers and a few dedicated tenants. AcmeCorp reported timeouts. Revenue-impacting? small fraction but replicated across many routes so tail latencies rising. anya: error rate spike: 0.4% -> 2.7% 5xxs on text-generation endpoints. Autoscale partially absorbing traffic but paging is increasing cost and causing extra latency. alex: can we get a quick snapshot of KV sizes by model and quant path? running query on telemetry now. eng_oncall: paste of telemetry snippet: ``` model awq-int8 avg_kv_bytes -> 3.2MB (baseline fp16: 0.9MB) model gptq-4bit avg_kv_bytes -> 1.1MB overall cache_entries -> +420% vs yesterday disk paging rate -> 5.3k/sec (baseline 420/sec) ``` devon: that matches my local reproducer — AWQ int8 currently stores kv as 32-bit aligned blocks due to kernel layout, so footprint ~3-4x. opsbot: deploy-bot: `deploy/infra/quant-kernel/awq-int8` rolled out 2026-03-14T02:12Z to us-west-2 lily: immediate mitigations we can try in parallel: - rollback awq-int8 kernel to previous kernel variant on affected nodes (fast) - lower continuous batching max_batch_tokens / increase batch timeout to force smaller kv lifetimes - reduce per-pod kv_cache_max_entries temporarily - route traffic away from affected capacity to fallback region (canary only) alex: I'll prepare a rollback. devon, can you test a quick config change: set kv_cache_max_entries=500 and batch.max_tokens=1024 on a small subset? want to see if eviction stabilizes. devon: doing that now on canary pool id=c-cache-02. will watch evictions and p95. [5m later] devon: canary results: evictions dropped 72%, p95 down to ~300ms (from 1.8s), paging rate down to 900/sec. Looks promising. lily: recommend full rollback of awq-int8 on all serving nodes in us-west-2 and apply temporary kv_cache_max_entries=800 cluster-wide until we fix kernel. anya: notifying impacted customers now. pinged AcmeCorp support and put status update on status.redwood.example. pagerduty: @pagerduty incident assigned to eng-sre oncall — high severity. eng_oncall: initiating rollback now. Command: ``` kubectl -n inference set image ds/quant-kernel quant-kernel=quant-kernel:v2026.03.13-prev --selector=region=us-west-2 ``` opsbot: rolling restart triggered. patch applied to 12/24 pods so far. expected 8m to complete. [10m later] alex: rollback completed across us-west-2. metrics slowly normalizing. p95 at 160ms, paging back to baseline, evictions normalized. devon: rolling back also restored previous kernel selection path; need to investigate why awq-int8 caused duplicate cache allocations when certain kernels fallback to host path. likely a kernel metadata mismatch bug. lily: status update for customers: "Mitigated — rollback of recent quant/kernel change. Moving to monitoring mode. :white_check_mark: alex: handoff: i'm off in 25m. lily, can you take primary for postmortem + customer comms? I'll add notes to incident doc. lily: taking handoff. I'll open postmortem draft and assign follow-ups. immediate action items: - add regression test for kv footprint across quant paths (int8/awq/gptq) with realistic prompts - add telemetry alert for sudden avg_kv_bytes increase (>2x baseline) - add canary gate for kernel rollouts that measures KV footprint on canary nodes before full rollout - consider adding memory-friendly kernel path that enforces 4bit packing for kv anya: also add a runbook tweak: when paging spike + eviction churn, prefer kernel rollback + tighten batch config as first steps. devon: i'm going to reproduce kernel layout discrepancy locally and submit a PR to kernel selection to avoid duplicate allocations. will include instrumented flags. alex: quick note — we saw continuous batching config amplified the issue. longer-lived large batches kept larger kvs resident. we should consider defaults that cap per-session kv retention when using aggressive quant paths. lily: agreed. final notes: incident duration ~1h 30m. impacted routes ~8% of production traffic, primary cause: AWQ-int8 kernel rollout caused KV footprint increase x3 on that quant path combined with continuous batching config leading to paging and evictions. Mitigation: rollback kernel + temporary kv/batch config adjustments. Next: postmortem, tests, canary gating, and customer follow-up. eng_oncall: handing off to lily for postmortem. tagging participants for follow-up: @devon @alex @anya @opsbot lily: acknowledged. I'll prepare postmortem doc and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to go over fixes. :calendar: end-of-thread-bot: thread closed for updates; reopen if metrics flare.

top_candidates.title: SRE Bot: INCIDENT CREATED — P1: KV cache growth + streaming token-cadence stalls observed in prod us-west-2. Alerts: high eviction rate on kv-cache + streaming partial-flush exceptions. Alyssa (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing a spike in 5xx for /v1/stream endpoints and multiple customer reports of streams that stop mid-token. Matt (eng-runtime): I can repro on canary. After the 14:08 deploy batcher config was changed: batch_max_tokens 2048 -> 4096 and prefetch=true. KV cache size growth ~3x on inference-03. Priya (eng-ml): Quick hypothesis — continuous batching increase + prefetching causes more aggressive KV key churn and paging. The streamer has a race where partial_flush() assumes KV entries exist; evictions can make kv_get() return null mid-stream => stalls. Kai (support): Customer impact: 4 PLG tenants reported ~40% failed streams in last 20m. No PII/data leak reported. Support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/1234 — customers requesting ETA. Alyssa (oncall): Immediate mitigations: rollback the batch_max_tokens change in canary, disable prefetch on affected fleets, and attempt a small defensive hotfix to the streamer. Rolling the rollback now. Deploy Bot: @Alyssa started deploy: rolling update config/continuous-batcher -> ci/continuous-batcher:rollback-20260315. 2/6 pods updated. Matt (eng-runtime): Also applying a temporary config cap to KV cache: lowering per-pod prefix cache from unlimited -> 8GB and bump eviction threshold to avoid paging cascade. Patch snippet: ```yaml batcher: max_tokens: 2048 prefetch: false kv_cache: max_memory_mb: 8192 eviction_policy: lru ``` Priya (eng-ml): I'll prepare a small runtime guard: if kv_get() returns null in partial_flush, schedule an async retry and skip the blocking path. Minimal change, unit tests passing locally. Jordan (product): Coordinating comms — drafting status page: "Degraded streaming for subset of customers; mitigation in progress." Will publish after we have rollback metrics. :eyes: Alyssa (oncall): Rollback metrics coming in — error rate dropped ~65% and streaming stalls reduced but we still see partial_flush exceptions on two pods (inference-03, inference-07). Matt (eng-runtime): Looking at stack traces: streamer::partial_flush() -> kv_get() -> null deref. Patch will add defensive null check + schedule retry with backoff. Also add tracing id to the flush path for correlation. Priya (eng-ml): Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming/pull/789 - includes defensive check + integration test that simulates eviction mid-stream. CI green. Can we push as patch release? Alyssa (oncall): Approved. @Matt please coordinate container build and deploy. Deploy Bot: build started for streaming/runner:v2.1.3-hotfix (triggered by @Matt). Deploy Bot: build success. rolling deploy streaming/runner:v2.1.3-hotfix — 1/4 pods updated and healthy. Kai (support): Customer-facing ETA updated to ~20-30 minutes. Notifying affected customers. Dedicated customers unaffected so far. Matt (eng-runtime): Enabling debug-level logs for partial-flush on the two suspect pods and attaching tracing. Also temporarily increase disk buffer for kv-cache on inference-03 in case paging recurs. Alyssa (oncall): Current status: mitigations applied (rollback + prefetch disabled + hotfix deployed). Impact reduced to ~10% failed streams across the cluster. Handing off to @Matt for monitoring and night coverage. Summary for handoff: - Root cause: continuous-batching config increase + prefetch led to KV cache blowup/paging. - Failure mode: paging triggered evictions during streaming; streamer partial_flush didn't handle null KV handles -> token cadence stalls/partial output. - Actions taken: rolled back batch_max_tokens, disabled prefetch, applied KV cache caps, deployed streamer hotfix to guard against null KV, enabled extra tracing. - Customer impact: Some PLG tenants affected; support notified; no data leak. - Next actions: monitor metrics and traces for 2h, run replay of affected traces, collect logs for postmortem. Matt (eng-runtime): Ack. I'll keep watch and escalate if anything regresses. Will also schedule a postmortem tomorrow and include replayed traces + config diff. Jordan (product): I'll draft the customer-facing postmortem and coordinate with CS for follow-ups. Alyssa (oncall): Thanks team :thumbsup: If any regression, tag SRE Bot with `incident escalate`. Switching channel to monitoring mode. SRE Bot: incident status -> monitoring. Escalation window: 2h. Assigned to Matt (oncall). top_candidates.title: title: Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF) — Launch & Operations Manual Overview This document describes the Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF), an opt-in program that supports cross-team skills development, rapid onboarding into adjacent domains, and internal mobility at Redwood. The RPF is a 6–12 week, project-oriented rotation designed for ICs and early managers who want hands-on experience in a different product area, platform team, or customer success track while keeping their core role and compensation intact. Purpose and goals - Accelerate skill acquisition for high-impact, cross-functional projects. - Reduce time-to-contribution when employees move to new teams or take on hybrid responsibilities. - Improve internal mobility rates and reduce hiring ramp costs. - Create repeatable handoff artifacts and templates that preserve institutional knowledge. Program variants - Short Fellowship (6 weeks): Focused learning sprint with one well-scoped deliverable. Best for tooling, docs, or experiment-driven work. - Standard Fellowship (9 weeks): Balanced discovery + delivery rhythm; includes a small end-to-end feature or migration task. - Deep Fellowship (12 weeks): For complex integrations, security/compliance projects, or multi-team migration planning. Eligibility and nomination - Who can apply: Regular ICs (L2–L5), staff-level engineers with manager consent, product managers, and member-of-staff customer success leads. - Manager approval: A written manager sign-off is required and must include a statement of support and a continuity plan for the fellow's home responsibilities. - Skill fit: Fellowship proposals must map to at least two measurable learning objectives and one deliverable for the host team. - Frequency: An individual may participate in the RPF up to twice in any 24-month period; exceptions require director-level approval. Key roles and responsibilities - Fellow (participant) - Own learning objectives, attend host team ceremonies, and deliver the agreed project artifact. - Maintain weekly updates to the home manager and host lead. - Home manager - Provide approval, maintain backfill plan (short-term coverage or task reprioritization), and maintain performance context. - Host lead - Assign a mentor, define the scope, and ensure access to systems and documentation. - Mentor (primary contact on the host team) - Provide day-to-day guidance, onboarding to codebase and tooling, and review deliverables. - People Ops (program owner) - Coordinate nominations, maintain fellowship schedule, run kickoff and wrap ceremonies, and keep program metrics. Selection process and timeline 1. Proposal submission (Week -3 to -2): Fellow or manager submits a 1-page proposal: goals, proposed host team, duration, and success criteria. 2. Triage (Week -2): People Ops validates eligibility and confirms host team capacity. 3. Approvals (Week -2 to -1): Home manager and host lead sign the rotation agreement. 4. Kickoff (Day 0): Program kickoff with People Ops, host mentor, fellow, and home manager. Agree on communication cadence, tooling access, and handoff milestones. 5. Midpoint check-in (Week 3–6): Formal review between the fellow, mentor, and home manager to adjust scope if needed. 6. Wrap & knowledge transfer (Final week): Document handoff, close tickets, and present outcomes at a cross-team demo. Rotation agreement template (1-page) - Title: [Fellow name] — [Host team] — [Duration] - Learning objectives: • Objective 1 • Objective 2 - Deliverable(s): • Artifact A (link) • Artifact B (link) - Duration and schedule: [start date] — [end date], expected weekly hours committed to host - Success criteria: 3 measurable acceptance checks - Approvals: Home manager | Host lead | People Ops Access and tooling checklist (example table) | Category | Items | Responsible | Target complete | |---------|-------|-------------|----------------| | Codebase | Repo access (read/write), CI runner tokens | Host lead | Day 2 | | Jira | Project write access, issue templates | Host lead | Day 2 | | Slack | Host team channel + #rpf-fellows | People Ops | Day 1 | | Cloud / Infra | Role-based access, test environment | Host lead + Security | Day 3 | | Analytics | Dashboard viewers, query access | Host lead | Day 4 | Onboarding & first-week cadence - Day 0: Kickoff meeting, rotation agreement sign-off, access checklist start. - Day 1–2: Codebase walkthrough, repo onboarding, run a local dev build, join host team standup and planning. - Day 3–5: Shadow mentor on core workflows, pick up first small task, weekly 1:1 scheduled with home manager and mentor. Performance management and compensation - The fellow remains on their home manager's org and payroll; there is no compensation change for standard rotations. - Performance feedback for the rotation is fed into the fellow's regular performance cycle by the home manager; the host lead provides a written rotation evaluation for the fellow's file. - Promotions and role changes resulting from the rotation are handled through standard promotion/transfer processes and require manager/director approval. Reporting, success metrics, and program KPIs People Ops will track and publish the following quarterly: - Fellowship count and completion rate (target completion >= 90%). - Average time to first meaningful contribution on host team (target <= 3 weeks for 6–9 week rotations). - Internal mobility conversion: percent of fellows who transfer roles within 12 months (target 18%+). - Fellow satisfaction (post-fellow NPS; target >= 8/10). - Document artifact quality: percent of handoffs with complete docs and runbooks (target >= 95%). Knowledge capture and handoff requirements - Every fellowship must close with a Confluence handoff page located under: /confluence/teams/[host-team]/rpf-handoffs/[fellow-name]-YYYYMMDD. - Required artifacts: - Architecture decision notes or design doc - Runbooks for anything operated in production - Test plan and known failure modes - A clear list of tickets left open and who will own them post-rotation Budgeting and perks - People Ops maintains a small rotation budget for cross-team learning. Typical reimbursable items include conference passes (pre-approved), short dedicated training, and workspace ergonomics for a remote fellow. - Fellows are eligible for a one-time learning stipend (up to $800) to cover books, courses, or small equipment purchases, pending manager sign-off. - Hosts can request a temporary headcount shadow (up to 2 weeks) for critical backfill; approvals routed through People Ops. Risk management and security - Sensitive projects (PII, audited) require a security review prior to approval. Host lead must list data accesses and sign off with Security. - If a rotation overlaps scheduled on-call windows, explicit contingency coverage must be documented before Day 0. - Hosts are responsible for ensuring fellows follow the host team's incident escalation and access policies. metadata.title: title: Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF) — Launch & Operations Manual Overview This document describes the Project Rotation Fellowship (RPF), an opt-in program that supports cross-team skills development, rapid onboarding into adjacent domains, and internal mobility at Redwood. The RPF is a 6–12 week, project-oriented rotation designed for ICs and early managers who want hands-on experience in a different product area, platform team, or customer success track while keeping their core role and compensation intact. Purpose and goals - Accelerate skill acquisition for high-impact, cross-functional projects. - Reduce time-to-contribution when employees move to new teams or take on hybrid responsibilities. - Improve internal mobility rates and reduce hiring ramp costs. - Create repeatable handoff artifacts and templates that preserve institutional knowledge. Program variants - Short Fellowship (6 weeks): Focused learning sprint with one well-scoped deliverable. Best for tooling, docs, or experiment-driven work. - Standard Fellowship (9 weeks): Balanced discovery + delivery rhythm; includes a small end-to-end feature or migration task. - Deep Fellowship (12 weeks): For complex integrations, security/compliance projects, or multi-team migration planning. Eligibility and nomination - Who can apply: Regular ICs (L2–L5), staff-level engineers with manager consent, product managers, and member-of-staff customer success leads. - Manager approval: A written manager sign-off is required and must include a statement of support and a continuity plan for the fellow's home responsibilities. - Skill fit: Fellowship proposals must map to at least two measurable learning objectives and one deliverable for the host team. - Frequency: An individual may participate in the RPF up to twice in any 24-month period; exceptions require director-level approval. Key roles and responsibilities - Fellow (participant) - Own learning objectives, attend host team ceremonies, and deliver the agreed project artifact. - Maintain weekly updates to the home manager and host lead. - Home manager - Provide approval, maintain backfill plan (short-term coverage or task reprioritization), and maintain performance context. - Host lead - Assign a mentor, define the scope, and ensure access to systems and documentation. - Mentor (primary contact on the host team) - Provide day-to-day guidance, onboarding to codebase and tooling, and review deliverables. - People Ops (program owner) - Coordinate nominations, maintain fellowship schedule, run kickoff and wrap ceremonies, and keep program metrics. Selection process and timeline 1. Proposal submission (Week -3 to -2): Fellow or manager submits a 1-page proposal: goals, proposed host team, duration, and success criteria. 2. Triage (Week -2): People Ops validates eligibility and confirms host team capacity. 3. Approvals (Week -2 to -1): Home manager and host lead sign the rotation agreement. 4. Kickoff (Day 0): Program kickoff with People Ops, host mentor, fellow, and home manager. Agree on communication cadence, tooling access, and handoff milestones. 5. Midpoint check-in (Week 3–6): Formal review between the fellow, mentor, and home manager to adjust scope if needed. 6. Wrap & knowledge transfer (Final week): Document handoff, close tickets, and present outcomes at a cross-team demo. Rotation agreement template (1-page) - Title: [Fellow name] — [Host team] — [Duration] - Learning objectives: • Objective 1 • Objective 2 - Deliverable(s): • Artifact A (link) • Artifact B (link) - Duration and schedule: [start date] — [end date], expected weekly hours committed to host - Success criteria: 3 measurable acceptance checks - Approvals: Home manager | Host lead | People Ops Access and tooling checklist (example table) | Category | Items | Responsible | Target complete | |---------|-------|-------------|----------------| | Codebase | Repo access (read/write), CI runner tokens | Host lead | Day 2 | | Jira | Project write access, issue templates | Host lead | Day 2 | | Slack | Host team channel + #rpf-fellows | People Ops | Day 1 | | Cloud / Infra | Role-based access, test environment | Host lead + Security | Day 3 | | Analytics | Dashboard viewers, query access | Host lead | Day 4 | Onboarding & first-week cadence - Day 0: Kickoff meeting, rotation agreement sign-off, access checklist start. - Day 1–2: Codebase walkthrough, repo onboarding, run a local dev build, join host team standup and planning. - Day 3–5: Shadow mentor on core workflows, pick up first small task, weekly 1:1 scheduled with home manager and mentor. Performance management and compensation - The fellow remains on their home manager's org and payroll; there is no compensation change for standard rotations. - Performance feedback for the rotation is fed into the fellow's regular performance cycle by the home manager; the host lead provides a written rotation evaluation for the fellow's file. - Promotions and role changes resulting from the rotation are handled through standard promotion/transfer processes and require manager/director approval. Reporting, success metrics, and program KPIs People Ops will track and publish the following quarterly: - Fellowship count and completion rate (target completion >= 90%). - Average time to first meaningful contribution on host team (target <= 3 weeks for 6–9 week rotations). - Internal mobility conversion: percent of fellows who transfer roles within 12 months (target 18%+). - Fellow satisfaction (post-fellow NPS; target >= 8/10). - Document artifact quality: percent of handoffs with complete docs and runbooks (target >= 95%). Knowledge capture and handoff requirements - Every fellowship must close with a Confluence handoff page located under: /confluence/teams/[host-team]/rpf-handoffs/[fellow-name]-YYYYMMDD. - Required artifacts: - Architecture decision notes or design doc - Runbooks for anything operated in production - Test plan and known failure modes - A clear list of tickets left open and who will own them post-rotation Budgeting and perks - People Ops maintains a small rotation budget for cross-team learning. Measurement and continuous improvement - People Ops will run bi-annual retrospectives with host leads and a representative set of fellows to iterate on the program. - The RPF handbook will be updated annually or following significant process changes. top_candidates.title: sam: Hey team — quick sync: we have a customer on Dedicated who hit capacity and got routed to Hosted, but the model variant on Hosted was a smaller quantized variant and the outputs were subtly different. Customer flagged it as a data-sensitivity concern. How should we handle routing when variant compatibility isn't exact? :thinking: elaine: Ugh. Was that routed by the current "tiered-fallback" policy? I thought Dedicated tenants could opt-out of spillover to Hosted. sam: They did not opt-out. Default is allow_spillover = true for mid-tier. They expected functional parity though. ravi: Two quick axes: (1) policy surface (console + API) vs org defaults, (2) telemetry/traceability so we can show customers what variant served them. We should fail closed if strict_isolation=true and otherwise attach routing_reason. alex: +1 on routing_reason. We also need a compatibility matrix check at routing time: if hosted variant model.arch != dedicated.model.arch or quant != quant we should either (a) refuse, (b) degrade gracefully with explicit header, or (c) fall back to a compatible hosted variant. Which is preferred? maria: For regulated customers, default should be refuse (reject) unless they explicitly allow variant-relaxed fallback. For mid-market, maybe allow but mark in console and send audit event. sam: Implementation idea: add a pre-routing hook that emits an event: {tenant, requested_variant, candidate_variant, compatibility_score, routing_decision}. Console shows per-request the last routing_decision and a link to the eval set used. Example event payload we could emit: { "tenant_id": "acct_ABC", "requested_model": "redwood/dedicated-xl-v2", "candidate_model": "redwood/hosted-xlq-quant", "compatibility_score": 0.72, "routing_decision": "spillover_with_variant_warning" } ravi: We should keep the schema minimal but searchable in logs. Suggest fields: routing_reason, variant_delta (enum: arch_mismatch, quant_diff, seq_len_limit), compatibility_score, override_flag. elaine: UX question: where does the customer configure this? Console toggle per-tenant + API field per-request? We need both. Per-request override should be rate-limited and audited. alex: Console affordance: add a toggle "Allow variant-relaxed spillover" (off by default for enterprise). Also surface last N routed requests with their routing_reason and compatibility_score. Add a big red badge when any routed request had variant_delta != none. maria: Also need a billing note: if the hosted variant has different perf/cost, we should surface potential cost delta on console and in invoice events. ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolled out routing_reason field to staging at 2130001100. Watch logs: /staging/routing/events sam: Nice. Edge-case: what if dedicated capacity is available but slow; should we prefer lower latency hosted variant over a busy dedicated? We currently route by priority: dedicated > hosted, but we could route by expected tail latency vs SLO. ravi: We can compute expected_latency = queue_time + p95_inference for variant. Add a policy expression: route_if(expected_latency(hosted) < expected_latency(dedicated) * 0.9 AND compatibility_score >= 0.9). That lets us choose hosted for latency-sensitive bursts. elaine: That policy sounds powerful but complex. Need to expose a safe default and a "policy editor" for advanced teams. Also need simulation UI: show hypothetical routing outcomes for last 24h. alex: Telemetry: add a tag on token-level logs: "served_variant" and "requested_variant", plus a trace_id linking request->fallback decision path. This makes debugging customer-reported regressions possible. maria: Ops-wise, we must ensure hosted variants serving PII-sensitive tenants are not used unless allowed. Add check: tenant_data_classification != pii OR allow_relaxed_spillover = true. sam: Action items: - [ ] add routing_reason, variant_delta, compatibility_score to routing events (ravi+alex) - [ ] console toggle and history UI (elaine+maria) - [ ] per-request API override + audit (alex) - [ ] default policy change for enterprise tenants to refuse (sam) - [ ] billing exposure for variant cost delta (maria) - [ ] add simulation in Console for policy changes (elaine) ravi: I'll draft the event schema tonight and post here. Also adding a small proposal for the compatibility_score heuristic: match on architecture, tokenizer, quantization, and output-stability evals. sam: Thanks. Let's keep default behavior conservative: reject for high-sensitivity customers, otherwise allow with warning and strong telemetry. :thumbsup: ops-bot: note: follow-up doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/routing/variant-fallback-proposal (draft)

top_candidates.title: ana: quick thought — proposal to relax embeddings endpoint so clients can send mixed-dim arrays if they opt in via header. router would split into uniform sub-batches and route per-model. avoids a lot of 413 churn for multi-model clients. sam: how do we bill/charge for splits? we'd need predictable quota semantics or we'll get support tickets. ana: plan: bill per original item using the target model's unit price. for splitter-generated child requests we emit telemetry linking child -> parent ID so usage and billing are reconciled server-side. clients still see single response. jordan: worry: splitting adds overhead and hurts batching efficiency. our load tests for runtime splitter showed ~3% 95p token latency increase on p3-like nodes. meera: console/telemetry needs: show split_rate, avg_splits_per_request, and per-split latency histogram. also surface percentage of requests that had partial failures. we should add a column in per-route table: "split enabled". ana: implementation notes: ``` Header: X-Embeddings-Allow-Split: true Payload: { "inputs": [[...],[...]], "model": "embed-large" } Router: if mixed dims -> create child reqs grouped by dims -> forward Response: 200 + { "results": [...], "split_info": { "children": 3, "partial_failures": [] } } ``` sam: partial failures — do we return 207 Multi-Status or always 200 with per-item status? returning 207 breaks a lot of SDKs. meera: prefer 200 with per-item status array. then console can show failure rate. SDKs parse it as normal. jordan: canary suggestion: feature flag default-off for hosted; enable for dedicated customers by config first. tag telemetry: split_feature=canary-<id>. rollout only after we have split-aware batching in runtime. infra-bot: load-test comment: "splitter + per-child routing" increased CPU on router by 8% and added 0.5ms to median request path in our 50k req/s test. (perf-run id: perf/2026-03-12/43) sam: need billing docs change: if child fails we still charge for successful children. if parent-level timeout occurs before children finish we prorate recorded tokens. I'll draft language. meera: UX: add a small indicator on route details: "split enabled (canary)" and a histogram for split_count; add alert if split_rate > 10% and 95p latency regresses > 2x compared to baseline. jordan: I'll prototype router split + telemetry events this week. can follow this cf-branch: feature/embed-splitter. I'll post PR with perf numbers. ana: action items: jordan prototype, meera console metrics + alert rules, sam billing blurb, i'll write RFC and include traffic model + SLO targets. :thumbsup: sam: :thumbsup: thanks. can we also log a sample of original payloads that trigger split for 24h for debugging? redaction required. ana: yes — sample at 0.1% with PII redaction. will include in RFC. meera: ok, i'm adding telemetry fields: ["parent_request_id","child_request_ids","split_count","split_reason","split_enabled_flag"], will send schema. jordan: noted. I'll tag all child requests with parent_request_id and split_version. ana: cool. I'll open the RFC tomorrow and cc infra/product. end.
