top_candidates.title: alex: FYI — we need a quick cross-team sync on the new error taxonomy metrics before the canary rollout next week. main asks: consistent names, dashboard panels, and which signals the console will use for degraded-mode UX. maria: Agree. Biggest open questions: 1) What counts as a fallback vs degraded mode? 2) Do we emit per-model or per-route counts? 3) How do quotas feed into routing decisions (reject vs queue)? sam: For counting: suggest these metrics - runtime.error.timeout_total - runtime.error.5xx_total - runtime.oom_total - runtime.fallback.count - routing.quota.rejected_total - routing.quota.queued_current We should include labels: model, route, region, tier ingrid: +1. Also include a boolean label 'degraded=true' when we return a graceful fallback so dashboards can differentiate hard failures vs graceful degraded responses. ryan: Console/UX note: we want a single 'Reliability' card that shows 3 small panels: latency/timeouts, 5xx rate, fallback rate. Fallback rate should be normalized per successful responses AND per attempted requests — otherwise it confuses users. devex: For SDKs we can surface a simple API: client.metrics.increment("fallback", {model, route, reason:"cache_miss"}) and have server translate to runtime.fallback.count; but we need a spec for accepted labels. sam: Proposal for PromQL snippets to standardize panels: # fallback rate per minute per route sum(rate(runtime_fallback_count{route!="",region="$region"}[1m])) by (route) / sum(rate(requests_total{route!="",region="$region"}[1m])) by (route) # 5xx rate sum(rate(runtime_error_5xx_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(requests_total[route!=""][5m])) by (route) maria: Good. Need to decide aggregation for quotas. I propose: - routing.quota.rejected_total{route,quota_name} - routing.quota.queued_current{route} And an alert if rejected_total rate spikes > 0.5% of requests for 15m. ingrid: On the runtime side, OOMs are noisy. We should emit both container-ish OOMs and model-serve OOMs: runtime.oom_total{oom_type="container"|"model"}. That will help SRE triage. alex: Cross-team action items: - eng-runtime: emit the metrics listed with labels (model, route, region, tier, degraded, reason) - eng-platform: provide standardized PromQL and dashboard templates - console: wire the 3-panel reliability card and the alerting thresholds - devex: publish SDK metric helpers + label schema Can people ack and add owners? ryan: Console owner for wiring: ryan — will add panels and create a JSON dashboard template that can be parameterized by org and region. sam: runtime owner: sam — will start a PR to export the metrics with the agreed labels. I'll add instrumented places for fallback increments and OOM tagging. ingrid: SRE/infra owner: ingrid — will verify OOM metrics and add a node-level fallback to ignore infra-level OOMs in the model-level graphs. devex: i'll own the SDK helpers and docs (devex). will open a spec doc with expected labels. maria: i'll own alerting thresholds and rollout plan for alerts (prod-safe gradual increase). will coordinate with ryan for console alert UI. alex: timeline: get metric exports by EOD Wed, dashboard/json templates by Fri, alert PRs early next week. if blockers surface, ping #eng-oncall and drop a short thread here. deploy-bot: milestone created: "reliability-metrics-rollout" assigned to alex, sam, ryan, ingrid, devex, maria ryan: quick UX question — do we want a per-route toggle in the console to hide low-traffic routes? otherwise the panel noise is bad. I propose default: show top 10 routes by request volume, with an expandable list. maria: yes please. also add breadcrumbs to go from a route panel to the model-specific timeline and the request traces link. alex: perfect. last ask: include an example payload spec in the dashboard doc for how the console will fetch aggregated metrics (time window, group_by labels, top_k param). devex/sam can pair on that. sam: noted. i'll include example API contract in the PR: /api/internal/metrics/aggregate?from=...&to=...&group_by=route,model&top_k=10 devex: ack, pairing session thursday morning? ryan: ack, thursday 10am works. i'll draft dashboard skeleton before then. ingrid: i'll run a short loadtest to ensure the new counters don't regress runtime perf; will report any cardinality issues. alex: thanks everyone — let's follow up in the PRs. cc @oncall if anything spikes during rollout.

top_candidates.title: incident-bot: PAGER — high 5xx rate for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 (automated detection). Alert severity: HIGH. Paging on-call. maria_g: acked, jumping in. seeing ~25% errors, latency spike to 2.1s p95. devon_s: on it — I'm pulling routing metrics and smart-routing decision logs. sre_lead: quick checklist: (1) scope customers impacted (2) confirm whether fallbacks triggered (3) validate DNS/edge. maria_g: customer-impact quick note: traffic to hosted-api eu region. Some requests routed to a model variant tagged `gptt-2-small` which we decommissioned last week — that could explain validation errors. eng_prod: wait, why would smart-routing pick `gptt-2-small`? policy should prefer matching model-tag then fallback to nearest region. Did a policy change go out? devon_s: pulling policy history... found a config push 45m ago that updated fallback chain for eu -> global -> us-east. looks normal. but routing logs show requests for eu being resolved to endpoint eu-edge-old.rwd.ai (decom) maria_g: DNS check from a few edge nodes: `dig +short eu.service.rwd.ai` -> returns CNAME to `eu-edge-old.rwd.ai` for some resolvers, `eu-edge-new.rwd.ai` for others. inconsistent. TTLs on the old records were 1h. ops_bot: system note: CDN invalidation completed 2h ago for eu-edge-new, but DNS change didn't propagate fully — looks like resolver caches holding old CNAME. sre_lead: hmm that explains routing loop: old edge is returning a healthy route but it's connected to retired compute pools referencing the old model variant. Smart-routing sees endpoint up -> routes -> inference fails -> fallback triggers -> routes again -> oscillation. devon_s: logs snippet: ``` [router] decision: prefer eu-edge-old.rwd.ai -> send to host 10.12.3.45 [host] model-check: variant gptt-2-small not available -> error 422 [router] fallback: route -> global-edge-1 -> global-edge-1 resolves back to eu-edge-old via DNS ``` maria_g: mitigation plan step 1: prevent routing loops by temporarily locking fallback policy to prefer-primary-region and disable circular fallback for eu for next 30m. Can someone apply? eng_prod: I'm applying the policy lock now via console and CLI. `redwoodctl routing set-policy eu --fallback-policy prefer-primary --disable-circular-true --note "incident 1782102468"` eng_prod: done. policy change rolled out to routers (prop 1). sre_lead: step 2: reduce DNS TTLs to 30s and force purge old CNAMEs from known public resolvers where possible. ops, can you coordinate with CDN/DNS provider? ops_bot: contacting provider support (ticket #CDN-58421). Meanwhile forcing purge on CloudEdge: `cloudedge purge eu-edge-old.rwd.ai` -> response: queued. devon_s: writing a query to count affected requests by origin resolver: `select count(*) from router_logs where region='eu' and upstream_host='eu-edge-old.rwd.ai' and status>=500 since -60m` -> ~43k requests. Error rate ~22% overall for region. maria_g: customer impact estimate: ~3.5% of total hosted API customers saw increased error rates for ~46 minutes. Noting a few high-volume customers reported 5xx spikes. sre_lead: good. step 3 rollback: point any smart-routing entries referencing `eu-edge-old` to `eu-edge-new` immediately. eng_prod, can you push a route override? eng_prod: pushing route override: `redwoodctl routing override set --host eu-edge-old.rwd.ai --target eu-edge-new.rwd.ai --ttl 60` -> rolled to all routing proxies. maria_g: verifying with `curl -v https://eu.service.rwd.ai/health` from multiple nodes — now resolves to eu-edge-new for 9/10 nodes, last one still showing old -> waiting for purge. devon_s: also noticed in traces that fallback policy was mis-evaluating model-variant compatibility because of a mapping file `/etc/redwood/model_variant_map.json` on the old pool that included `gptt-2-small`. That file should have been removed during decommission. sre_lead: assign owner to clean decommission artifacts: tim_k take point with infra to ensure no stray mapping files remain on retired pools. tim_k: on it — kicking a job to sweep retired pools. `infra-cleanup --tag retired --check model_variant_map.json` -> queued. ops_bot: CDN purge completed for most POPs. provider reports positive propagation but some ISP caches still stubborn. maria_g: continuing monitoring. error rate trending down — now 7% and falling. p95 latency back to 450ms. devon_s: while we recover, recommend we keep the fallback lock for +30m and leave override in place for +60m. Also drop DNS TTL change to 15s if still flapping. sre_lead: agreed. extended locks applied. also opening an RCA ticket and a customer-impact tracker. please add any customers that submitted support tickets. eng_prod: adding quick mitigation note to status page: "Partial degradation for EU-hosted inference endpoints; mitigation in progress. No data loss; temporary routing policy enforced." :warning: maria_g: handoff to next on-call in 30 minutes. summary for oncall-next: root cause is stale DNS/CNAME pointing some resolvers to decommissioned edge which had leftover model variant mapping producing validation errors, creating fallback oscillation. Mitigations applied: routing fallback lock, route override to eu-edge-new, CDN purge, infra sweep for mapping artifacts. oncall-next: reading and acking. will monitor for the next 2 hours and coordinate with support for customer follow-ups. sre_lead: timeline note (for postmortem): first alert at 1782102468, policy change/override at 1782102760, CDN purge effective 1782103380, rolling recovery starting 1782103600, incident declared resolved for customers at 1782106000 but monitoring will continue. maria_g: closing slack updates — will paste postmortem link once created. great job team :thumbsup: incident-bot: Incident auto-log: created incident-2026-08-xx-1782102468, severity=high, tag=smart-routing,dns,edge,ttl."

top_candidates.title: maya: Heads up — after we pushed the 535.86 driver + CUDA 12.2 roll last night, we've got a regression: NVLink topology isn't being detected on mixed A100 nodes. NCCL falls back to SHM -> SOCKET for most peer transfers, huge perf hit. leo: which cluster/region? maya: prod-gpu-eu, also seeing on staging-us-west. Only on racks that have a mix of kernel versions (5.15.x + 6.1.x) and some older A100-SXM nodes. taylor: any logs or nccl topo dump? short snips are fine. maya: paste: ``` $ nvidia-smi topo --matrix GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 CPU GPU0 X NV PHB SYS GPU1 NV X PHB SYS GPU2 PHB PHB X SYS ``` but nccl shows: ``` NCCL INFO Topo: NVLINK not usable between 0 and 1 (p2p query failed) NCCL WARN All-to-all using SOCKET fallback for peer 0-1 NCCL INFO SHM disabled (IPC failure) ``` indra: SHM disabled often due to IPC namespace or missing /dev/shm mount in container. Are these in k8s pods with ipcMode? any change in runtime flags? maya: pods are default, we didn't change --ipc. Container runtime didn't update, only driver and kernel modules. dmesg on one node: ``` [ 428.123456] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: P2P peer lookup failed, peer 0000:3a:00.0 [ 428.123460] nvidia-mig: failed to query P2P capability ``` jun: Could be the kernel driver ABI mismatch — mixing dkms-built modules with packaged driver? Which package mechanism did we use for 535? rpm or runfile? maya: runfile installer (we used for faster rollout). Some older nodes still had kernel module from 525 and we forced install but didn't rebuild DKMS properly. leo: that explains P2P failures. If module symbols mismatch, NVLink P2P ioctl can fail and NCCL disables p2p. Workaround: put affected nodes into maintenance and roll back to 525, or rebuild kernel module via dkms and reboot. taylor: timeline wise, can we isolate by node label and cordon? Also we should avoid full rollback if we can hotfix: rebuild modules and restart kubelet + container runtime to rebind devices. maya: doing a canary: cordoned 2 nodes in prod-gpu-eu and initiated dkms rebuild + reboot. I'll report perf after. ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0783 - "NVLink/NCCL P2P regressions after 535 driver rollout". Pager on-call: leo, taylor. indra: another mitigation: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 to force consistent path (explicit SOCKET) while we fix drivers — avoids random mixed behavior, but costs throughput. Also NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1 if IPC is flaky. jun: note: forcing SOCKET may hurt multi-node perf but keeps correctness; useful temporary flag for training jobs that can't tolerate nondeterministic fallbacks. maya: perf numbers after canary rebuild: peer bandwidth for single-GPU pairs went from 3.2 GB/s (socket fallbacks) back to 72 GB/s when NVLink restored. Good sign. taylor: good. Next steps: - create an automated check during driver rollout: run `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` + `nccl-tests` smoke to validate NVLink/SHM - add DKMS verification in rollout playbook - add node label to identify kernel-driver mismatches maya: I'll open a PR to update the rollout runbook + add a k8s admission job that checks /dev/shm and ipc namespace for GPU pods. leo: also add a step: if module version mismatch detected, mark node drainable and block burst autoscaler from placing new GPU pods. maya: noted. will follow up with timeline and postmortem notes. srebot: Deploy log: driver-rollout-2025-03-22 completed on 2025-03-22T02:13:00Z. 17 nodes patched, 4 nodes reported dkms mismatch. maya: thanks — tagging this thread for postmortem. Any objections to rolling back the remaining 3 mismatched nodes to 525-runfile and re-testing before reapplying 535 via dkms package? taylor: +1. safer and we can automate dkms-based rollout afterwards. leo: please include cost impact estimate in postmortem (retries + slower jobs). I expect ~12% longer training time for affected jobs in EU yesterday. maya: will include. closing the loop when PR/PM posted.

top_candidates.title: incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P0 - multi-GPU TP job hang detected. Alert: nccl_collective_deadlock. Affected job run/infra/tp-infer-9. NCCL observed 'comm abort' on rank 3 -> peer disconnect. Nodes implicated: gpu-node-134, gpu-node-135. Triggered at 2026-03-15T03:02:58Z. Paging #incidents and eng-runtime oncall. mike: Ack, I'm oncall. Pinging @sara and @jaya for TP/NCCL help. Can someone grab pod logs and node dmesg? Hypothesis: OOM or GPU driver reset causing comm abort. sara: grabbing logs now. I see CUDA error on gpu-node-135: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" inside the container runtime-gt-45. NCCL logs show repeated "ncclRecv: Connection reset by peer" and then comm abort. Snippet: ``` [2026-03-15T03:02:57Z] rank 3: NCCL WARN Unhandled cuda error at src/comm.c:412 [2026-03-15T03:02:58Z] rank 3: CUDA kernel abort: illegal memory access [2026-03-15T03:03:00Z] rank 3: ncclCommAbort called ``` mike: thanks. Can you check kubelet/container status and the node dmesg for OOM or driver resets? Run `kubectl describe pod runtime-gt-45 -n runtime` and `ssh gpu-node-135 sudo dmesg | tail -n 200`. sara: `kubectl describe` shows container state: Terminated (OOMKilled) at 03:03Z. dmesg shows an OOM kill: "Out of memory: Killed process 22456 (python)" and also a GPU driver reset entry: "nvidia: GPU reset: Xid 31". So looks like the container hit a memory limit and the driver reset followed, which explains the NCCL disconnect. jaya: I'm on it. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl-hang. Immediate mitigation: isolate the offending node, restart affected containers on healthy nodes, and trigger routing fallback to single-GPU model variant for the route. We should also limit max batch size temporarily. mike: executing node isolation: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-135 && kubectl drain gpu-node-135 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Drain started at 2026-03-15T03:08:12Z. oncall-bot: Escalation update: mike -> jaya at 2026-03-15T03:10:05Z. frank: customer-success note: Customer A (dedicated us-west-2) reported latency spikes starting 03:04Z, ~12 failed inference requests in last 10m, some retries succeeded. Please confirm impact so we can prepare a customer message. mike: confirmed customer impact: 12 timed-out requests, no inference outputs lost (retries hit fallback and succeeded). Marking customer impact as P1 for CS notification. Will draft a brief. sara: restarted container runtimes on other nodes and repro'd OOM when batch size > 8 in internal test. Logs point to a potential memory regression introduced in kernel module of model-variant v1.13. Rolling back route to model:v1.12 (single-GPU) via console rollout. Example API call used: `POST /routes/route-123/rollout { \"target\": \"model:v1.12\", \"strategy\": \"immediate\" }`. jaya: also applied temporary autoscaler throttling and batch cap (max_batch=8) for the affected route. Created INF-3021 to track root cause and driver-team coordination. Collecting core dumps from gpu-node-135 before we reprovision. eng-sre: created incident ticket INC-4212345678 and PD alert PD-38291. Archiving logs to s3://redwood-incidents/4212345678/. mike: short summary: mitigation in place - node drained, container restarts completed on healthy nodes, routing fallback to single-GPU model active, temporary batch cap set, customer impact limited to ~12 timed-out requests, no data loss. Handing off incident to @jaya for RCA and postmortem follow-up. My oncall shift ends in ~2h. jaya: taking post-incident. Next actions: collect GPU core dumps, upload to S3 path above, coordinate with drivers team for Xid 31 investigation, run regression tests against model:v1.13, update runbook with a new check for container memory regressions, and prepare RCA + customer communication template. mike: closing live coordination thread. :white_check_mark:

top_candidates.title: oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert: incident PAGER-8243 triggered for cluster inference-prod. Symptoms: sudden spike in NCCL communicator errors and multi-GPU hangs, repeated container restarts on nodes gpu-12,gpu-13,gpu-17. Error rate > 20% for /v1/generate on model-xlarge-8way. Paging sre oncall now. sre_jamie: Ack. I'm on it. Can folks paste the latest pod logs for the failing rank? I want the first glimpse of the NCCL stack. ml_infra_lee: Pasting trimmed log from pod inference-runtime-xyz (rank 2): ``` [2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL WARN Unhandled cuda error, aborting [2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL ERROR ncclCommAbort called, communicator invalid [2026-03-15 02:45:21] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error' runtime_error: cudaLaunchKernel failed: out of resources at /workspace/runtime/collective/comm.c:412 at /usr/local/bin/inference-runtime ``` We're also seeing container restarts (`CrashLoopBackOff`) and occasional OOMs on the GPU when sequence length spikes. eng_omar: Likely bad interaction between kernel scheduling and tensor parallel communicator. Could be a race on communicator teardown when a pod gets preempted. Quick mitigation: reduce tensor-parallel degree for active model-route and shift traffic to a smaller single-gpu variant. I'll prepare route change if SRE gives go. sre_jamie: Immediate mitigation plan (proposed): 1) Temporarily mark the 3 problematic nodes unschedulable (cordon) to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 gpu-13 gpu-17`. 2) Drain the failing pods and restart the runtime on healthy nodes: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl delete pod -l app=inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-12` for each. 3) Apply fallback routing: shift 40% of traffic for model-xlarge-8way to model-xlarge-1gpu (lower throughput, safe single-gpu path). 4) If restarts persist, scale model instances down to TP_SIZE=1/PP_SIZE=1 for the route and restart the deployment. ml_infra_lee: Executed step 1 & 2 on gpu-12 and gpu-13. Logs show one node had `nvidia-driver` OOM trace and GPU driver process got killed. I cordoned gpu-17 but didn't drain yet (still serving). Sample command I ran: ``` kubectl cordon gpu-12 kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-xyz-2 ``` cs_tara: Any idea which customers hit 5xxs? AcmeFinance just flagged errors in prod. Need ETA to share with them. ml_infra_lee: From metrics: AcmeFinance and BetaRetail were the top two that hit elevated 5xx counts. Total user-facing error rate peaked ~18% on the route. After cordon+drain the error rate dropped to ~6% but still above baseline. eng_omar: I'm ready to change routing. If SRE confirms the partial reroute, I'll do a canary 20% -> 80% to test stability. sre_jamie: Do it. eng_omar make it 25/75 for 10 minutes, watch latency and error stream. deploy-bot: Routing update started by eng_omar: model-xlarge-8way -> 25% traffic to model-xlarge-1gpu. Rollout id: r-20260315-1759 ml_infra_lee: After routing shift we saw error rate go to ~2-3% but latency increased on the single-gpu path as expected. No more NCCL communicator aborts on nodes still serving. Meanwhile, pod restarts have stopped on gpu-12 and gpu-13. ops_maya: I suggest we also enable NCCL debugging envs on a staging replica to capture more info: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL`. Also consider setting `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` briefly to rule out p2p prob. sre_jamie: Good call. But don't flood prod logs. Run debug on a single canary pod in a non-customer shard. ml_infra_lee: Created a debug deployment `inference-debug-canary` with NCCL_DEBUG enabled and TP/PP set to same as prod. Collecting traces now. sre_jamie: Next steps for live mitigation: keep nodes cordoned, maintain 25/75 routing split, finish draining gpu-17 if safe, and run a controlled rollout with TP_SIZE=1 for model-xlarge across the cluster if we see reoccurrence. Also open a ticket for post-incident capacity adjustments. cs_tara: Sending a short customer update: "We're investigating elevated errors on model-xlarge; traffic has been partially rerouted to a stable variant and we're working on node restarts. ETA 1h for remediation" — ok to send? sre_jamie: OK to send. Add note that some customers may see higher latency. pagerduty: On-call handoff: sre_jamie -> ops_maya at 03:15 UTC. Handoff acknowledged. PagerDuty note: continue mitigation, collect debug logs, and escalate to HW vendor if driver kills persist. ops_maya: Took over. Running NVIDIA diagnostics on gpu-17 now (`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CEC,PERSISTENCE`). One node shows ECC corrected errors increasing. ml_infra_lee: ECC counts rising on gpu-17, and dmesg shows multiple `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` entries. I queued a maintenance for that host with infra: HOST-REPLACE-178. eng_omar: Given suspected hardware instability, we should automate fallback routing for high-latency/5xx spikes in future: if error-rate > 5% for 2m, automatically shift 50% traffic to single-gpu variant. Filing an RFC after mitigation. sre_jamie: Agreed. For now: drained gpu-17 and replaced 2 pods onto healthy nodes. Error rate back to baseline ~0.8%. We'll keep the cluster at reduced TP config overnight and schedule full postmortem. deploy-bot: Rollout complete: r-20260315-1759 -> routing now 10% single-gpu, 90% original (rollback in case of symptoms). All health checks green. ops_maya: Marking incident as mitigated. Creating a follow-up task: replace gpu-17 host, validate ECC and driver stability, and run a soak test for 6 hours with TP_SIZE=2. sre_jamie: Closing incident PAGER-8243 as mitigated. Action items: (1) Postmortem + timeline (owner: ml_infra_lee), (2) Auto-fallback RFC (owner: eng_omar), (3) Hardware replacement and soak (owner: ops_maya). I'm adding these to the incident ticket. cs_tara: Thanks team — will update AcmeFinance and BetaRetail that we've mitigated and will follow up with timeline and RCA. oncall-bot: Incident PAGER-8243 status -> mitigated. Incident postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC.

Marta (eng-sre): Suggest we do a hotfix patch release to canary then run extended soak 1h, then if clean we can merge to main with revert or keep guard. Also a bunch of instant 502s from gpu-farm-12. sre_tony: canary hosts showing model variant mismatch on a node: config shows expected `m-7b-q8` but runtime pulled `m-7b-fp16` on one machine. that could explain memory/latency mismatch. maya: wait how would that happen? the artifact repo only has q8. Could be a packaging tag mixup between the image and model manifest. ops_jess: grabbing fetch logs from artifact-store: `manifest.json` for canary contains `variant: q8_0` but the node reported `variant: fp16` while kernel was compiled for q8. unpack failure leads to degraded perf. lee: impact: ~10% of requests hitting canary cluster see p95 4.8s and 502s. customer_success_ana: CSMs report a couple of enterprise customers saw degraded chat for a few minutes and one filed a support ticket. product_sam: this aligns with a rollout policy we changed last week to sticky_sessions=true for canary to get consistent evaluation. sticky made many active sessions stick to the bad canary. sre_tony: sticky_sessions is the issue. because of sticky routing, retries went back to canary rather than fallback. fallback_policy allowed region fallback but sticky prevented immediate distribution. we ended up with increased pressure on fallback pool. ops_jess: observed an emergent fallback loop: canary marked unhealthy -> traffic routed to fallback variant in the same region -> fallback overloaded -> fallback triggers its own fallback to cross-region -> sticky flags cause controllers to bounce sessions around. net effect: oscillation and elevated latency cluster-wide. lee: I'm going to pause the canary rollout and flip sticky to false for the route. executing: ``` # rollback command redwoodctl deploy rollback --id 1769994300 --to 1769900001 --scope canary ``` maya: handing this to night oncall (maya) in 10 minutes, lee please provide full timeline in the incident ticket. I'll stay on until it's stable. lee: copying timeline here: 1769994300 canary started, 1769998765 alert fired, 1769998780 sticky traffic observed, 1769998802 patch applied, 1769998810 rollback initiated, 1769998820 rollback complete and canary drained. customer_success_ana: CSMs notified affected customers at 1769998830 with temporary mitigation note and ETA for full root cause. sre_tony: short term mitigation summary: paused canary, disabled sticky sessions on affected route, rolled back canary model variant, increased fallback pool capacity by +2 nodes. This stopped the oscillation. will open a follow-up to prevent mismatch between model manifest and runtime image. product_sam: action items: (1) disable sticky by default for canaries unless perf-sensitive test requires it, (2) add manifest-image checksum check on deploy pipeline, (3) add canary health gating for KV cache alloc before proceed. maya: I'm taking over monitoring. setting watch for 2h. assigning postmortem to lee + ops_jess + deploy infra. severity: P2 (customer-facing but quick mitigation). lee: will file incident ticket with timeline, customer impact (error rate ~10% for ~7m for 3% of traffic, 2 enterprise customers flagged), and root cause hypothesis: variant packaging mismatch + sticky sessions exacerbated fallback loop. oncall-bot: Incident 1769998765 updated: status -> mitigated. next: postmortem scheduled 2026-03-17 14:00 UTC. :white_check_mark: customer_success_ana: added support ticket links to incident. I'll follow up with customers once postmortem is ready. :thumbsup: maya: thanks all. keep replies to thread for the ticket notes. I'll @-mention SRE rotation for the postmortem.

I'm seeing traffic imbalance to a subset of edge nodes in us-east1. Repro rate ~2.5% 5xx. raj: I'm looking at LB logs. There's a sudden connection queue depth on the east ingress. Could be slow downstream responses. mike: Runs: `curl -sS https://edge.east.health/metrics | jq '.connections'` shows many TIME_WAITs. Suspect connection churn to cache/backends. leila: Can we do a graceful failover to us-central while we investigate east? We should validate first with a synthetic canary. anne: Yes. Plan: create quick synthetic job in us-central to validate a few endpoints, then shift 30% traffic for 5m, watch p95 & 5xx, then increase. infra-bot: Command: `traffic-shift start --from=us-east1 --to=us-central1 --pct=30 --duration=5m --validate=synthetic-canary` ops-bot: Synthetic canary job `smoke-canary-us-central` created and executed: 10/10 requests OK, avg latency 210ms. raj: Canary good. Initiating shift. mike: Noting KV-cache miss rate in us-east1 increased by ~3x. Adding cache replica to east and throttling new connections from bursty clients. leila: Live mitigation: cache scaled +2, outbound connections for pool east-7 restarted to clear stuck connections. anne: After shift p95 in east dropped from 1.3s -> 780ms, 5xx dropped by 60%. Good. Holding shift at 70% to central to confirm stability. raj: Quick customer-impact note: a handful of sessions dropped between 20:05-20:12 UTC. Support ticketing group notified. leila: For follow-up: alert tuning needed - current latency alert fires on 1m window which causes churn. Propose: change latency -> 5m rolling p95 and require sustained deviation. Also add region-specific thresholds. mike: Suggest adding a Prometheus recording rule for regional p95 to speed queries and avoid flapping: ``` - record: regional:request_p95:5m expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region)) ``` leila: Also add an alert: `RegionalHighP95` with for: 10m, labels: severity=page if region QPS > baseline*0.2 else severity=warn. That reduces noise for low-traffic regions. raj: We should dedupe pages coming from multiple monitors for the same root cause (e.g., cache pressure). Proposing a new alertmanager grouping rule: group_by: ['cluster', 'region', 'alertname', 'cause_signature_hash'] anne: Add suppression during automated rollouts and traffic shifts to prevent paging for expected transient latencies. We can use a silence when `traffic-shift` flag is active. infra-bot: Applied temporary 30m suppression tag `in-progress-traffic-shift` to related alerts. ops-bot: Creating ticket INF-4602: "Alert tuning + multi-region failover dashboard" assigned to eng-infra. Will include suggested recording rules, alert changes, and grouping rules. leila: Dashboard work: need a side-by-side panel showing traffic proportion, regional p95, 5xx rate, cache miss rate, and instance health. Panel IDs we'll include in the ticket: 112, 113, 114, 115. mike: Also recommend a small alert pipeline: first-level warning to #monitoring for 5m, escalate to oncall if persists 10m. Mike take the recording rules & alerts. Raj take the dashboard. mike: I'll prototype the alert changes in staging and run a sensitivity sweep for false positives. Will post results. ops-bot: Incident timeline saved to incident-doc: https://redwood-internal/incidents/1802238890 (private) anne: Oncall handoff: I'll hand primary to raj in 90 minutes. Leaving detailed mitigations in the doc. raj: Taking handoff. Leaving a short checklist: monitor `regional:request_p95:5m`, `kv_cache_miss_total`, `tcp_time_wait_count`, and `edge_5xx_rate`. If any trend > 2x baseline, re-escalate. incident-bot: Incident resolved: auto-close after mitigation verified. time_to_ack: 2m, time_to_recover: 14m. Tags: regional-failover, alert-tuning, synthetic-canary leila: Quick retro note: need better pre-emptive canary coverage for all critical API paths. Adding INF-4604 for canary coverage expansion. anne: Good job team. After action: we'll run a tabletop next week focusing on cross-region failover and alert noise reduction.

Connections spike and active conn saturates Nginx worker. Samir Patel: any customer-facing impact? which routes most affected? Maya Rivera: highest is /v1/embed and some chat streaming routes. Affected customers: a handful of high-volume tenants saw errors and retried -> increased load. NOC Bot: Detected elevated 502/504s at 10:02 UTC. Notified oncall. Maya Rivera: initial hypothesis: origin instances overloaded => proxy returns 502s; possible connection LMDB thrash from kv-cache layer causing increased p99 service time. Alice Chen: rolling healthcheck shows origin instance count stable, but CPU spike on two hosts and slow socket close times. Carlos Gomez: mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily divert traffic away from the busiest instance backends, 2) enable connection_reuse_timeout tweak on edge, 3) increase max_conns on proxy pool, 4) enable degraded-mode fallback for embed route (serve cached embeddings) for 10m. Samir Patel: +1 on degradations for embed if it reduces errors. We should notify impacted customers. Observing drop in errors from some nodes. Maya Rivera: p50 improved slightly, p99 still elevated. Errors down to 3.2% overall. Carlos Gomez: deploying degraded fallback for /v1/embed: switch to cached response path. Patch: ```yaml routes: - path: /v1/embed fallback: cache-first cache_ttl: 300 ``` Carlos Gomez: toggled fallback flag via console feature flag `embed_degraded_mode=true`. Samir Patel: please add a short customer notice to status page and Slack customer channel. Maya Rivera: posting to status page: "Investigating elevated 5xx rates affecting embedding and streaming routes in US-WEST. Mitigations in progress." Maya Rivera: current stats: overall 5xx 3.1%, embed-specific 6.8% -> after fallback embed 5xx down to 1.4% for requests hitting fallback. Alice Chen: telemetry shows origin pool-2 still noisy — connection resets persist. I'm going to cordon the two problematic hosts and rotate them out of LB. infra-oncall: temporary cordon scheduled. Running `kubectl cordon node-09 node-11` and `drain` with graceful timeout. Alice Chen: cordon + drain done for node-09, traffic rebalanced. Node-11 draining now. Maya Rivera: monitoring: after node-09 drain, p99 latency dropped ~18%, 5xx dropped another 0.8 percentage points. Carlos Gomez: also added a short-term nginx keepalive tweak: `keepalive_timeout 10s; keepalive_requests 100;` to reduce stale connection pile-up. Maya Rivera: good. Are there any config regressions that would cause this post-deploy? Any recent rollouts? Carlos Gomez: no full rollouts in the last 2 hours. There was a config push yesterday but benign. I see an increase in retries from a particular internal job that runs hourly — that amplified pressure. Samir Patel: we'll follow up with the product owner to throttle that job. Can someone open a ticket? Maya Rivera: created ticket #INC-2026-1842: "Investigate internal heavy retry job causing origin pressure". Assigned to Platform Tools. NOC Bot: Noted. Customer-impact log: - 12 customers saw increased error rate >1% for >5m - No full outage, intermittent errors, automatic retries mitigated some traffic Samir Patel: drafting customer message: "We experienced intermittent 502/504 errors in us-west affecting embeddings and streaming requests between 10:02-10:18 UTC. Alice Chen: handing off active mitigation to night oncall at 02:00 UTC. leaving playbook notes in the channel and runbook updated. Maya Rivera: handoff checklist posted. Maya Rivera: final note: recommend postmortem focusing on (a) why internal retry job wasn't throttled, (b) why origin pool didn't autoscale sooner, (c) better circuit-breaker thresholds on edge. Samir Patel: agreed. I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem. incident-bot: Incident SEV2 closed for active mitigation at 10:48 UTC — monitoring continue. Please file postmortem within 72 hours. Maya Rivera: closing channel for active triage. If anything regresses ping @infra-oncall and escalate to oncall-engineering.

combined with continuous batching, the runtime's batching logic ends up fragmenting microbatches under lock contention -> more RPCs and evictions. kevin: customer-signal: support got multiple tickets about slow responses and timeouts for embedding jobs for large customers around 09:12. impact: elevated latency and a few 500s for high-concurrency customers. alice: mitigation plan (short term): 1) throttle incoming concurrency for affected pools, 2) disable prefetch heuristic on prod-cluster-7, 3) increase microbatching timestep window slightly to allow bigger batches. maria: agree. quick change: flip `PREFETCH_HEURISTIC=off` in env for pool slot-a and slot-b, and set `MICROBATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=8` -> currently 4. Should reduce fragmentation. jamal: prepared a one-line hotpatch — ready to apply after sanity checks: ``` kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cont-batch-runtime PREFETCH_HEURISTIC=off MICROBATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=8 --record ``` alice: go for it. I'll run canary first on slot-c (low-traffic) then scale to slot-a/b if metrics look good. ops-bot: deploybot: Starting rollout: set env for deploy/cont-batch-runtime -> canary slot-c (1 pod). (1m later) alice: canary metrics - queue_delay.p99 down 40%, evictions/sec down 85% on canary pod. microbatch size median increased from 1 to 5. Looks promising. jamal: rolling to slot-a/b now. I'll keep concurrency throttle in place: per-tenant qps limit for customers tagged 'high-burst' set to 60% of usual for next 30m. kevin: notifying impacted customers: sending template update to XYZ and a note to support queue that we're mitigating with config hotpatch, ETA 20m for full rollout. alice: rolling completed. monitoring across prod-cluster-7: p99 latency trending down toward baseline. still seeing a handful of timeouts from long-tail tenants. maria: digging into root cause follow-up: we should add a guard to prefetch heuristic to avoid prefetching more than N prefixes per tenant under high concurrency and to coordinate with the microbatching backpressure signal. filing an RFC/bug. jamal: quick note for oncall handoff - leaving in 30m: current state = mitigated (config off + throttle), customer impact = reduced latency, some residual 500s clearing. follow-up work: revert heuristic or make it concurrency-aware, add telemetry to correlate prefetch volume -> evictions. alice: handoff to jamal in 25. docs updated in incident channel. kevin: support: sent proactive messages to 3 customers, logging ticket IDs: #7892 #7893 #7894. asked customers to retest. maria: postmortem items I'm adding: - Revert or patch prefetch heuristic: limit per-tenant prefetch under concurrency. - Add runtime feature flag to dynamically disable prefetch under high evictions. - Add alert that triggers when microbatch median falls below 2 AND prefetch rate > threshold. - Add dashboard linking per-tenant request fanout -> KV footprint. ops-bot: pagerlog: incident 4367890000 marked mitigated at 4367890280 by alice. jamal: taking over oncall. leaving token: `handoff:jamal` — I'll monitor 1h and then update postmortem draft. any remaining actions for night? alice: nothing urgent; just ensure the throttle is kept until the heuristic patch is live or we revert the change. kevin: customers confirmed improved perf for 2 of 3. will close tickets once fully verified. maria: creating follow-up ticket and assigning to infra-team: INFRA-2026. attaching traces and logs. jamal: thanks team. putting this in the oncall log and incident board. if anything regresses ping me directly or escalate to @pagerduty. :thumbsup: (End of thread)

Elevated 95/99 p90 latency and OOM-ish eviction churn. auto-triage: possible correlation with last night’s quant/kernel rollout to awq-int8 variant. alex: seeing it on dashboards too. p95 gen latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.8s for a subset of routes. paging reads/sec up ~10x, disk IO saturated on multiple pods. :eyes: devon: root cause hypothesis: AWQ int8 kernel increases KV cache per-entry size due to different kv layout + kernel selection fallback causing duplicate caches. Combined with continuous batching config (max_batch_tokens=2048) we might be retaining much bigger KV for long-lived sessions. lily: customers affected: heavy-chat customers and a few dedicated tenants. AcmeCorp reported timeouts. Revenue-impacting? small fraction but replicated across many routes so tail latencies rising. anya: error rate spike: 0.4% -> 2.7% 5xxs on text-generation endpoints. Autoscale partially absorbing traffic but paging is increasing cost and causing extra latency. alex: can we get a quick snapshot of KV sizes by model and quant path? running query on telemetry now. eng_oncall: paste of telemetry snippet: ``` model awq-int8 avg_kv_bytes -> 3.2MB (baseline fp16: 0.9MB) model gptq-4bit avg_kv_bytes -> 1.1MB overall cache_entries -> +420% vs yesterday disk paging rate -> 5.3k/sec (baseline 420/sec) ``` devon: that matches my local reproducer — AWQ int8 currently stores kv as 32-bit aligned blocks due to kernel layout, so footprint ~3-4x. opsbot: deploy-bot: `deploy/infra/quant-kernel/awq-int8` rolled out 2026-03-14T02:12Z to us-west-2 lily: immediate mitigations we can try in parallel: - rollback awq-int8 kernel to previous kernel variant on affected nodes (fast) - lower continuous batching max_batch_tokens / increase batch timeout to force smaller kv lifetimes - reduce per-pod kv_cache_max_entries temporarily - route traffic away from affected capacity to fallback region (canary only) alex: I'll prepare a rollback. devon, can you test a quick config change: set kv_cache_max_entries=500 and batch.max_tokens=1024 on a small subset? want to see if eviction stabilizes. devon: doing that now on canary pool id=c-cache-02. will watch evictions and p95. [5m later] devon: canary results: evictions dropped 72%, p95 down to ~300ms (from 1.8s), paging rate down to 900/sec. Looks promising. lily: recommend full rollback of awq-int8 on all serving nodes in us-west-2 and apply temporary kv_cache_max_entries=800 cluster-wide until we fix kernel. anya: notifying impacted customers now. pinged AcmeCorp support and put status update on status.redwood.example. pagerduty: @pagerduty incident assigned to eng-sre oncall — high severity. eng_oncall: initiating rollback now. Command: ``` kubectl -n inference set image ds/quant-kernel quant-kernel=quant-kernel:v2026.03.13-prev --selector=region=us-west-2 ``` opsbot: rolling restart triggered. patch applied to 12/24 pods so far. expected 8m to complete. [10m later] alex: rollback completed across us-west-2. metrics slowly normalizing. p95 at 160ms, paging back to baseline, evictions normalized. devon: rolling back also restored previous kernel selection path; need to investigate why awq-int8 caused duplicate cache allocations when certain kernels fallback to host path. likely a kernel metadata mismatch bug. lily: status update for customers: "Mitigated — rollback of recent quant/kernel change. We’re performing a deep postmortem and will follow up with timeline and remediation steps." :thumbsup: incident-bot: SEV2 -> Mitigated. Moving to monitoring mode. :white_check_mark: alex: handoff: i'm off in 25m. lily, can you take primary for postmortem + customer comms? I'll add notes to incident doc. lily: taking handoff. I'll open postmortem draft and assign follow-ups. immediate action items: - add regression test for kv footprint across quant paths (int8/awq/gptq) with realistic prompts - add telemetry alert for sudden avg_kv_bytes increase (>2x baseline) - add canary gate for kernel rollouts that measures KV footprint on canary nodes before full rollout - consider adding memory-friendly kernel path that enforces 4bit packing for kv anya: also add a runbook tweak: when paging spike + eviction churn, prefer kernel rollback + tighten batch config as first steps. devon: i'm going to reproduce kernel layout discrepancy locally and submit a PR to kernel selection to avoid duplicate allocations. will include instrumented flags. alex: quick note — we saw continuous batching config amplified the issue. longer-lived large batches kept larger kvs resident. we should consider defaults that cap per-session kv retention when using aggressive quant paths. lily: agreed. final notes: incident duration ~1h 30m. impacted routes ~8% of production traffic, primary cause: AWQ-int8 kernel rollout caused KV footprint increase x3 on that quant path combined with continuous batching config leading to paging and evictions. Mitigation: rollback kernel + temporary kv/batch config adjustments. Next: postmortem, tests, canary gating, and customer follow-up. eng_oncall: handing off to lily for postmortem. tagging participants for follow-up: @devon @alex @anya @opsbot lily: acknowledged. I'll prepare postmortem doc and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to go over fixes. :calendar: end-of-thread-bot: thread closed for updates; reopen if metrics flare.
